The file contains no state variables, no actions, no temporal specification, and no proofs; it appears to serve as a minimal model-checking or helper module that adds concrete values on top of definitions from the extended module without defining any behavior of its own.

536.specification: This module specifies a nondeterministic algorithm for computing the maximum element of an input integer sequence drawn from a constant set Tuples, with the special case that the maximum of the empty sequence is minValue. The PlusCal algorithm repeatedly chooses an index from the remaining index set I, updates max when inp[i] > max, and removes that index from I until all positions have been examined; the translated TLA+ model includes a terminating stuttering action after pc = "Done". The specification assumes every tuple element is greater than minValue, uses weak fairness on Next, and asserts both termination and the correctness condition that the final max is either minValue for the empty tuple or else equals some input element and is at least every input element.

537.specification: This module defines simple model-checking properties for a specification imported from Session6. It introduces a concrete constant set, a partial-correctness condition relating the final program counter state to the computed square, a typing invariant over the state variables, and a stronger reachable-state invariant characterizing the values of x and i for each control location. The file does not define its own transition system or temporal specification, and it contains no fairness conditions, proofs, or PlusCal algorithm.

538.specification: This module specifies a simple iterative algorithm that computes the square of a chosen natural number n by repeatedly adding successive odd numbers. The PlusCal algorithm initializes x and i to 0, then loops while i < n, incrementing i and updating x by adding 2*i - 1; the translated TLA+ actions model the control flow using the variable pc. The spec assumes NSet contains natural numbers, allows infinite stuttering after termination to avoid deadlock, and verifies a temporal termination property stating that eventually pc reaches "Done".

539.specification: This module is a model-checking companion module for a specification imported from Session6func. It defines several state predicates and invariants about a simple computation that fills an array or function x with squares of indices from 0 through n, with control state pc ranging over "a", "b", and "Done". The file asserts a postcondition for correctness when pc = "Done", a typing invariant for n, x, i, and pc, and a stronger reachable-state invariant that characterizes what must hold in each control location.

540.specification: This specification models a simple PlusCal algorithm that computes successive square values by iteratively updating an array x. The algorithm starts with x[j] = 0 for all j in 0..n, then repeatedly increments i and sets x[i] to x[i-1] + (2*i - 1), which is the standard recurrence for squares. The generated TLA+ translation defines the control state pc, a terminating stuttering action to avoid deadlock after completion, and checks a temporal termination property asserting that eventually pc reaches "Done". There is no explicit fault model; this is a deterministic single-process computation.

541.specification: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around a specification imported from the Session7 module. It defines a single top-level property, AddCorrect, stating that if processes "ProcA" and "ProcB" are both in the "Done" control state, then the variable x equals 2. The file itself introduces no variables, actions, or temporal specification; it only extends another module and asserts a state-level correctness condition over imported identifiers.

542.specification: This specification models a simple PlusCal algorithm with two processes, ProcA and ProcB, that both increment a shared variable x once. The translated TLA+ spec uses a program-counter variable pc to track each process's control location, initializes both processes at their single statement, and then allows either process action to execute until both reach "Done". The specification checks the standard safety-style behavior through the transition relation and includes a temporal termination property asserting that eventually all processes are done; it also permits infinite stuttering after termination via an explicit Terminating action to avoid deadlock.

543.specification: This module is a small model-checking companion module for a specification extended from Session7fg. It defines a concrete constant value, a type correctness invariant over the state variables x, pc, and t, and an additional correctness condition stating that if all processes are in the "Done" control state then x equals N. It also defines the set of distinct process pairs and a mutual exclusion style invariant asserting that no two different processes can simultaneously be in control states "p1" or "p2", which appear to represent a critical-section region.

544.specification: This specification models a PlusCal algorithm in which N concurrent processes increment a shared variable x by 1 using a binary semaphore sem for mutual exclusion. Each process repeatedly follows the translated control flow lock, p1, p2, and unlock, storing the shared value temporarily in a local per-process variable t before writing back x := t[self] + 1. The spec assumes N is a positive natural number, defines the standard initial condition and next-state relation from the PlusCal translation, permits infinite stuttering after all processes reach Done to avoid deadlock on termination, and asserts a temporal termination property that eventually every process reaches Done.

545.specification: This module is a simple model-checking wrapper around an imported mutual exclusion specification, apparently selecting the Session8peterson module rather than alternative commented-out candidates. It defines a concrete process count of 3 and a corresponding process index range 0..(ConstN-1), and states a mutual exclusion property over the imported state variables Procs and pc. The file does not define its own transition system or temporal specification, but instead adds concrete constants and a safety assertion intended to be checked against the extended Peterson-style protocol model.

546.specification: This specification models a simple round-robin mutual exclusion style protocol generated from a PlusCal algorithm named Alternate. A single shared variable turn determines which process may leave its waiting location and enter the critical section, and each process cycles through noncritical, enter, critical, and exit control states recorded in pc. The spec assumes a positive number of processes indexed by Procs = 0..(N-1), defines the initial state and next-state relation, and verifies behavior with a basic temporal specification Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars without explicit fairness or separate safety/liveness theorems.

547.specification: This module specifies a one-bit mutual exclusion protocol for N processes, originally written in PlusCal and translated into TLA+. Each process repeatedly cycles through noncritical section, entry, critical section, and exit, using a shared boolean flag array and a local index j to scan other processes and wait when contention is detected. The specification includes the initial state, per-process actions, a global Next action, and the temporal specification Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars.

548.specification: This specification models the N-process Peterson mutual exclusion algorithm as a PlusCal algorithm translated into TLA+. Each process repeatedly cycles through noncritical section, entry protocol, critical section, and exit, using the shared arrays level and last_to_enter to coordinate access to the critical section. The file defines the initial state, one action per translated control location, a combined Next action over all processes, and a simple temporal specification Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars; it does not include explicit fairness, liveness, or proof obligations.

549.specification: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around another specification, Session9alt. It defines concrete model values for the number of processes and the process set, and adds two temporal properties over the inherited state variable pc: a mutual exclusion safety property stating that no two distinct processes are simultaneously in the critical section, and a naive liveness property stating that every process visits the critical section infinitely often. The file itself does not define the underlying algorithm or transition relation; it only adds these constants and property definitions on top of the extended module.

550.specification: This specification models a simple round-robin mutual exclusion protocol generated from a PlusCal algorithm named Alternate. A shared variable turn determines which process in Procs is allowed to enter the critical section, and each process cycles through control locations "ncs", "enter", "cs", and "exit". The temporal specification requires initialization, all behavior steps to satisfy Next modulo stuttering, and weak fairness for each process action procs(self), ensuring that every process that remains enabled eventually gets scheduled.

551.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper around an underlying one-bit mutual exclusion specification imported via EXTENDS Session9onebit. It introduces concrete model constants for three processes and states safety and liveness properties over the imported state variable pc, namely mutual exclusion, deadlock/livelock freedom in the sense that some process trying to enter eventually reaches the critical section, and starvation-freedom properties for processes 0 and 1. The file itself does not define the operational algorithm; instead it specializes the model with ConstN and ConstProcs and states temporal properties to be checked, including a comment noting that NoStarveProc1 is not satisfied by the algorithm.

552.specification: This specification models a one-bit mutual exclusion protocol for N processes, originally written in PlusCal and translated to TLA+. Each process repeatedly cycles through a noncritical section, raises its own flag, scans other processes, may back off if it sees a competing flag before its own turn, and eventually enters and exits a critical section. The spec assumes a nonempty process set Procs = 0..(N-1), uses weak fairness for each process when it is outside the noncritical section, and defines the overall behavior with Init, Next, and a temporal Spec formula.

553.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a Peterson-style mutual exclusion specification defined in the extended module Session9peterson. In this file, it introduces concrete constants for the number of processes and the process identifier range, and states two correctness properties: mutual exclusion and starvation freedom. The module itself does not define the algorithm steps directly, but it expresses that no two distinct processes are simultaneously in the critical section and that any process at location "enter" eventually reaches location "cs".

554.specification: This module specifies Peterson's N-process mutual exclusion algorithm, written as a PlusCal algorithm and accompanied by its TLA+ translation. The algorithm models a set of processes in Procs that repeatedly cycle through noncritical section, entry protocol, critical section, and exit, using shared arrays level and last_to_enter to coordinate access to the critical section. The specification assumes a positive number of processes with Procs = 0..(N-1), and it verifies behavior under weak fairness of each process action once the process has left the "ncs" control location.

555.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper around another specification, Session9sem, and adds concrete constants and temporal properties for a mutual exclusion protocol. It fixes the number of processes to 3 and defines the process set as the range 0..(ConstN-1). The module asserts mutual exclusion as a safety property, and also states deadlock/livelock freedom and starvation freedom as leads-to liveness properties over the process control-state variable pc.

556.specification: This specification models a simple semaphore-based mutual exclusion algorithm generated from a PlusCal algorithm named SemMutex. A set of processes repeatedly cycles through a non-critical section, waits until a binary semaphore has value 1, enters the critical section by setting the semaphore to 0, and then exits by restoring the semaphore to 1. The spec assumes a positive number of processes indexed by Procs = 0..(N-1), defines the translated control-state variable pc, and verifies behavior under a temporal specification with both weak fairness for non-ncs process steps and strong fairness for the enter action of each process.

557.specification: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around the DieHard specification. It defines fixed capacities for a small jar and a big jar, constrains the state variables to remain within those capacity bounds, and states a simple safety condition that the big jar is not equal to 4. The file contains only state-level definitions and no actions, temporal specification, fairness, proofs, or PlusCal algorithm content.

558.specification: This module specifies the classic Die Hard water-jug problem using two buckets of capacities 5 and 3. The commented PlusCal algorithm models a single process that repeatedly nondeterministically chooses among filling, emptying, and pouring actions between the buckets, and the translated TLA+ action FixWater captures those state transitions over the variables bigBucket, smallBucket, action, and water_to_pour. The specification defines an initial state and a temporal specification Spec as Init /\ [][Next]_vars, and it includes an invariant Inv asserting that bigBucket is never equal to 4.

559.specification: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around a Paxos Commit specification. It extends PaxosCommit, instantiates module TCommit as TCommitSpec, defines TCommitSpecProperty as TCommitSpec!TCSpec, and states the theorem that PCSpec implies TCommitSpecProperty.

560.specification: This module specifies the Paxos Commit algorithm, modeling resource managers, acceptors, leaders, and the set of all messages ever sent. It focuses only on safety, not liveness: messages are represented by membership in a global message set rather than explicit receipt events, leader selection is left abstract, and resource managers may spontaneously prepare or abort. The specification defines the protocol state, the actions of resource managers, leaders, and acceptors, a next-state relation and full temporal specification, and proves type correctness as well as that the protocol implements the transaction-commit specification imported from module TCommit.

561.specification: This module is a small model-checking companion module for the transaction commit specification defined in TCommit. It adds two top-level state predicates over the variable rmState: a type-correctness condition requiring each resource manager to be in one of the four named status strings, and a consistency condition stating that no two resource managers can simultaneously be in aborted and committed states respectively. The module itself does not define actions, temporal behavior, fairness, or proofs; it only introduces these state-level predicates while extending another module.

562.specification: This specification models the transaction commit protocol (TCommit) for a set of resource managers (RMs). Each RM can be in one of several states: working, prepared, committed, or aborted. The protocol allows RMs to prepare, commit, or abort a transaction, with actions defined for each transition. The specification checks that all RMs can only commit if all are prepared, and that abort is only possible if no RM has committed. The temporal property TCSpec asserts that the system starts in the initial state and all steps are valid transitions, using stuttering steps as needed. No explicit fairness or liveness properties are specified beyond the basic temporal structure.

563.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper around a two-phase commit specification. It defines a typing invariant for the resource-manager and transaction-manager state, imports a separate transaction-commit specification via INSTANCE, and states a theorem that the two-phase commit specification implies the imported transaction-commit property. The file itself contains no actions, no temporal specification definition of its own, and no fault model beyond what may exist in extended or instantiated modules, which are not extracted here.

564.specification: This specification models the Two-Phase Commit protocol, a classic distributed transaction commit protocol involving a transaction manager (TM) and a set of resource managers (RM). The model tracks the states of the resource managers and the transaction manager, as well as the set of messages exchanged between them. The protocol proceeds in two phases: first, RMs prepare and notify the TM, and then the TM decides to commit or abort, informing the RMs. The specification defines the possible actions for both TM and RMs, including preparation, commit, abort, and the receipt of messages. The temporal property TPSpec asserts that the system starts in the initial state and all steps are valid transitions according to TPNext. The model is parameterized by the constant RM, representing the set of resource managers, and does not explicitly model faults or failures.

565.specification: This module defines debugging, visualization, and state-alias operators for a Raft-related specification imported from the extended module ccfraft. It does not define the core protocol itself; instead, it builds aliases, colorized renderings, aggregate views, and TLC-driven instrumentation over the existing state variables and actions of the underlying model. The file uses CHOOSE, function and record constructors, sequences, and TLC extension operators to summarize leader elections, blocked nodes, per-node vote and message statistics, and animated log/state output for simulation traces.

566.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper around an underlying abstraction module, restricting the server set, term range, and log bounds to make exploration finite. It defines a concrete symmetric server set of three nodes, bounds terms to 2..4, sets the start term to the minimum of that range, and constrains log lengths via bounded sequences and an explicit length constraint. The file does not define a full temporal specification itself; instead it provides configuration-style helper operators and type constraints intended to be used with the imported abstraction, with symmetry reduction through permutations of the server set.

567.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper around a Raft-related specification, configuring and restricting the explored state space for a CCF/Raft model. It reads configuration choices from the IO environment, constrains reconfiguration sequences, term growth, client requests, message duplication, and signature generation, and defines debugging and coverage-related predicates for TLC runs. The file also introduces assumptions about configuration and term/request bounds, a symmetry set and view for model checking, and postconditions intended to detect whether certain debug invariants were ever exercised.

568.specification: This module specifies a network message buffer abstraction parameterized by a delivery guarantee. It models four network behaviors: ordered without duplication, ordered with duplication, reordered without duplication, and reordered with duplication, all selected by the constant Guarantee. The module defines how messages are initialized, added, removed, queried by destination and source, observed to increase, and nondeterministically dropped under each guarantee, using a single state variable messages.

569.specification: This module specifies a tiny simulation driver that runs an external TLC simulation command for another specification, apparently SIMccfraft, using the IOUtils community module. The state consists of a configuration record-like function c over fields R, C, Q, and T, each chosen from the set {10, 1000}, and a Boolean flag d that ensures the external command is executed at most once. The behavior initializes c to one of the allowed parameter combinations and d to FALSE, then Next performs a single step that prints the chosen configuration, executes the shell command built by CmdLine, requires the process exit value to be 0, sets d to TRUE, and leaves c unchanged; deadlock checking is disabled in the configuration block.

570.specification: This module defines a simulation-oriented wrapper around an existing ccfraft specification, adding randomized guards to selected actions, custom initialization choices, a redefined fairness condition, periodic TLC statistics serialization, and a postcondition module for counterexample shortening. The fault model is not introduced independently here; instead, the module reuses the underlying ccfraft behavior and constrains simulation scheduling through RandomElement-based throttling and IO-environment parameters. The specification also includes utilities for stopping TLC after a time budget, serializing runtime data, and a postcondition that records the depth of a discovered counterexample so TLC can be rerun in simulation mode with progressively smaller bounds.

571.specification: This module validates execution traces of a CCF Raft implementation against a Raft TLA+ model by reading a JSON trace log, filtering raft-related events, and constraining the model to follow those events step by step. It defines predicates that match concrete log lines to specific protocol actions such as timeouts, elections, append-entries exchange, configuration changes, and request-vote handling, while also accounting for implementation details such as piggybacked UpdateTerm behavior and possible message loss. The specification checks that the trace can be matched by the model, that the resulting states satisfy the underlying ccfraft invariants as state constraints, and includes temporal properties ensuring successful trace traversal and a reference specification for composed next-state behavior.

572.specification: This module gives an abstract specification of a distributed consensus algorithm in terms of commit logs maintained by a finite set of servers. The model assumes a strong observation model in which any node can atomically inspect the state of all other nodes, and it focuses on append-only logs that never diverge: servers may copy a suffix from another server, extend a longest log, or copy one of the longest logs and extend it. The specification defines an initial-state condition, a next-state relation over the single variable cLogs, and temporal safety-style properties such as append-only growth, absence of conflicting logs, and equivalence between existential action definitions and axiom-style formulations used for efficient refinement checking in TLC.

573.specification: This module specifies the CCF variant of the Raft consensus algorithm over an asynchronous message-passing network with explicit in-flight messages, per-server logs, terms, elections, reconfiguration, and retirement of nodes. It models CCF-specific features such as signatures that make prefixes committable, pre-vote behavior, configuration changes, retirement phases, and explicit successor nomination via propose-vote messages. The specification defines an initial single-node start configuration, a detailed next-state relation with message send/receive handlers, fairness assumptions over both node and network actions, and verifies a collection of safety and temporal properties including log consistency, append-only committed logs, refinement to an abstract spec, and several CCF-specific invariants about signatures, configurations, and retirement.

574.specification: This specification models consistency of an abstract transactional service with histories of client-visible request/response events and a set of ledger branches representing views. Read-write transactions can be requested, executed onto a branch, responded to with an observed prefix, and later receive committed or invalid status messages; read-only transactions observe a branch and receive a response carrying the observed sequence and transaction identifier. The model includes view changes via ledger truncation and branch extension, checks typing and committed-event structure, and asserts a basic temporal specification `Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars` together with state and temporal helper properties such as ledger monotonicity and a consistency invariant relating committed read-write responses to later committed read-only observations.

575.specification: This module defines a collection of state invariants over an external transaction history, for a system modeled in another module named ExternalHistory. The history contains read-write and read-only requests and responses, transaction IDs, observed transaction sequences, and transaction status events such as committed or invalid. The invariants characterize request/response ordering, uniqueness of transactions and transaction IDs, constraints on committed and invalid statuses, observation consistency, serializability, linearizability, and ordered speculative linearizability, along with a few debugging invariants that intentionally characterize special reachable states such as having no committed or invalid transactions.

576.specification: This module defines the externally observable client history for a transactional system in which clients can receive transaction responses before the transactions are committed. It models read-write and read-only transactions, transaction status notifications, and helper sets derived from the history to identify committed and invalid transactions and related request/response events. The specification focuses on typing and monotonicity properties of the shared history, using an append-only history variable and temporal assertion that the history always remains a prefix of its next-state value.

577.specification: This module defines an alternative initial state for a multi-node reads model by extending an existing base specification and adding a new initial predicate. The alternative state initializes ledger branches and history so that two transactions are already committed, as indicated by the comment and by the pre-populated response and committed-status records in the history sequence. The module then defines a temporal specification that starts from this alternative initial state and evolves according to the imported action MCNextMultiNodeReadsAction, using the standard stuttering form [][MCNextMultiNodeReadsAction]_vars.

578.specification: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper for a multi-node reads specification. It extends two other modules and adds a combined next-state action that allows either the underlying multi-node transition or read-only transaction request/response actions, then defines a standard safety-style temporal specification using Init and a boxed next-step formula. The file itself contains no local state declarations, constants, fairness, proofs, or PlusCal algorithm; it serves as a small composition layer over actions defined elsewhere.

579.specification: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper for a MultiNode specification by restricting part of the behavior with an explicit bound on the number of view changes. It extends existing modules and adds a constant ViewLimit, then defines bounded action variants that guard inherited actions with checks on the lengths of ledgerBranches and history. The module defines a combined next-state action and a temporal specification MCSpecMultiNode == Init /\ [][MCNextMultiNodeAction]_vars, but it does not introduce its own fairness, proofs, or PlusCal algorithm.

580.specification: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper around a single-node read system specified elsewhere. It adds history-bound guards to the read-only transaction request and response actions, and combines them with an existing single-node next-state action from another extended module. The temporal property defined here is a simple safety-style specification stating that the system starts in Init and then evolves according to the stuttering closure of MCNextSingleNodeReadsAction over vars.

581.specification: This module defines a bounded model-checking wrapper around a single-node specification by restricting some actions based on the length of the history. It extends another module and introduces one constant, HistoryLimit, to cap the number of events recorded in the history. The specification defines bounded variants of selected actions, combines them into a next-state relation, and asserts a standard temporal specification consisting of the imported Init predicate and a box-action formula over the bounded next action.

583.specification: This specification models a multi-node version of a CCF service by extending a single-node model with additional behavior for view changes and leader election. It introduces an action that simulates leader election by truncating uncommitted suffixes of a ledger branch and appending a new branch, and another action that sends invalid transaction status responses when a transaction can no longer be committed in the current or future views. The temporal property defines the system behavior as starting from Init and evolving according to NextMultiNodeAction under stuttering, with no explicit fairness or proof obligations in this module.

584.specification: This specification extends an existing SingleNode specification to model read-only transactions on a single-node system. It adds one action for submitting a read-only transaction request and another action for producing a response that observes the contents of some ledger branch, assuming read-only transactions are always forwarded and that the read and response occur in one atomic step. The temporal property defines the system behavior as starting from Init and then repeatedly taking NextSingleNodeReadsAction steps with stuttering allowed over vars.

585.specification: This specification models the externally visible behaviour of a single-node CCF service. It tracks an abstract external history of requests and responses together with abstract per-view ledger branches, and it assumes there are no view changes because only a single node is considered. The spec checks type correctness of the history and ledgers, defines append-only ledger monotonicity as a temporal property, and gives actions for submitting, executing, and responding to read-write transactions as well as reporting committed transaction status and appending unrelated transactions.

586.specification: This module defines a trace-validation wrapper around a separate MultiNodeReads specification. It reads a JSON trace log, steps through it line by line using a local variable l, and constrains system actions so that each modeled action must match the next logged event, while also permitting preparatory backfilling steps that do not advance the log. The specification additionally asserts an environment assumption for TLC execution in breadth-first, single-worker mode, defines a temporal trace-following spec over <<l, vars>>, and includes temporal properties intended to detect whether the entire trace was matched and whether that matching was non-trivial.

587.specification: This specification models a Percolator-style transactional storage protocol with primary and secondary keys, explicit locks, committed writes, rollback records, and cleanup of stale locks. Transactions progress through init, working, prewriting, committing, committed, or aborted states; they may read keys, prewrite locks concurrently, commit a primary key, or abort, while stale-lock cleanup may either roll back data or complete secondary-key commit based on the primary key's outcome. The spec verifies safety-oriented invariants including typing, write-order consistency, lock consistency, committed/aborted consistency, rollback consistency, and a snapshot-isolation monitor encoded with auxiliary variables.

588.specification: This specification models a system with three clients (c1, c2, c3) and three keys, where all clients share the same primary key. The comments indicate that the model is intended for TLC model checking, focusing on symmetry among clients due to their identical primary keys. The spec defines the sets of keys and clients, a mapping from clients to their primary key, and a symmetry set for model checking. No algorithm, actions, or temporal properties are defined in this file; it is likely intended as a configuration or parameterization for a larger system specified in the extended CollapseRollbacks module.

589.specification: This specification models a single-variable cyclic counter together with TLC-managed side effects through the TLCSet, TLCGet, and PrintT operators. The state variable x is initialized to 0 and the next-state action increments it modulo 5, while also updating a TLC tool value stored under key 42. The temporal specification requires the initialized behavior, all steps to satisfy the stuttering-closed next-state relation, and weak fairness of Next; it also states a liveness property that x repeatedly reaches 1, plus postconditions about the TLC tool state.

590.specification: This specification models a concurrent variant of the Percolator transaction protocol over a set of keys and clients. Each client executes a transaction with a primary key and secondary keys, using start and commit timestamps, prewrite locks, cleanup of stale locks, and commit of the primary key before secondaries are considered committed or recoverable. The model checks safety-style properties including typing invariants, write and lock consistency, committed and aborted transaction consistency, and an auxiliary snapshot isolation condition tracked by instrumentation variables.

591.specification: This specification models a simple concurrent percolator system for model checking with TLC. It defines three clients (c1, c2, c3) that all share the same primary key, making them symmetric for the purposes of the model. The symmetry set is explicitly defined using the Permutations of the Client set, and the module is intended for use with the ConcurrentPercolator and TLC modules. No temporal properties, actions, or state variables are defined in this file; it is primarily a configuration and symmetry setup for model checking.

592.specification: This module defines a very small parameterization for a concurrent percolator specification by fixing the key space to two keys and the client set to two concurrent clients. It models two clients, c1 and c2, whose primary keys are 1 and 2 respectively, and is intended for TLC model checking as stated in the comments. The file itself contains only constants and simple value definitions; it does not define variables, actions, temporal properties, fairness, or proofs, and it relies on an extended module for the actual system behavior.

593.specification: This specification models a distributed transaction protocol with both optimistic and pessimistic clients, inspired by TiKV/Percolator-style locking, prewrite, commit, rollback, and lock resolution behavior. The model represents requests as a monotonically growing set of sent messages and models responses as direct atomic client-handling actions, explicitly abstracting away in-transit response delivery while retaining enough history to verify safety properties. It focuses on safety rather than liveness, including type correctness, commit/abort consistency, lock/write consistency, uniqueness properties, message timestamp consistency, and snapshot isolation for both optimistic and pessimistic transactions; stale-lock cleanup is modeled via check_txn_status and resolve messages, with TTL abstracted as always expired when checked.

594.specification: This module defines a small configuration for a distributed transaction system, likely for testing or demonstration purposes. It declares two keys and three clients, and then defines sets and mappings that specify which clients are optimistic or pessimistic, which keys each client can read or write, and the primary key for each client. The module does not define any actions, temporal properties, or proofs, and serves as a parameterization or configuration layer for the system specified in the DistributedTransaction module.

595.specification: This module defines a concrete instantiation of part of a distributed transaction model by introducing specific key and client constants and several derived constant mappings. It classifies three clients into optimistic and pessimistic categories, assigns each client its read and write key sets, and identifies a primary key for each client. The file does not define variables, actions, temporal behavior, fairness, or proofs; it is a static configuration-style module layered on top of an extended module.

596.specification: This module specifies a one-variable transition system in which x starts at 0, can move nondeterministically from 0 to either 1 or 2, and from any nonzero value returns to 0. The main specification is an initial condition together with the temporal formula [][Next]_x and a weak fairness condition WF_x(Next), so the behavior is constrained by stuttering-closed next-state evolution plus fairness for Next. The file also states temporal properties about eventually stabilizing away from 1 or 2, eventual repeated return to zero, the negation of one temporal property, and a postcondition that checks a TLC-generated counterexample trace encoded as records, tuples, and sets.

597.specification: This specification defines a trivial one-variable TLA+ module with a single state variable x. It includes an explicit contradictory assumption, `TRUE = FALSE`, noted by a comment indicating the contradiction is intentional. The only behavioral property defined is `Spec`, which requires the initial state to satisfy `x = 0` and thereafter allows only stuttering steps via `[][UNCHANGED x]_x`.

598.specification: This module provides a concrete instantiation of a distributed transaction model by defining specific keys and clients for a test scenario. It extends the external module DistributedTransaction and the TLC module, and introduces constants for three keys and three clients, then defines sets and client-to-key mappings for optimistic and pessimistic clients, read sets, write sets, and primary keys. The file itself contains only static top-level value definitions and no state variables, actions, temporal specification, or proof content; any transactional behavior is inherited from the extended module and therefore is not extracted here.

599.specification: This specification models an optimized transactional commit protocol in the style of Percolator with primary and secondary keys, per-key locks, versioned writes, and transaction timestamps. Clients move through init, working, prewriting, committing, committed, or aborted states; they can read keys, clean up stale locks, prewrite locks on keys, commit the primary key, or abort. The model checks type correctness and several safety properties including write ordering, lock consistency, committed/aborted consistency, rollback consistency, and preservation of a snapshot-isolation indicator tracked explicitly in the state.

600.specification: This specification models a system with three concurrent clients (c1, c2, c3) operating on a single table with three keys. All clients share the same primary key, which is set to 1 for each client, indicating symmetry among them. The spec is intended for TLC model checking, as noted in the comments, and leverages symmetry reduction by defining a symmetry set over the clients. The module extends OptimizedCommitTS (presumably containing the main protocol logic) and TLC (for model checking support). No temporal properties, actions, or proofs are defined in this file; it serves as a configuration and parameterization layer for the underlying protocol.

601.specification: This specification models a simple system with two clients and a table with two primary keys, intended for TLC model checking. The clients are represented by the constants c1 and c2, and each client is associated with a unique primary key (1 or 2) via the ClientPrimaryKey mapping. The module does not define any actions, temporal properties, or proofs, and serves as a basic setup for further modeling or as a configuration for model checking scenarios.

602.specification: This specification models Google's Percolator-style distributed transaction protocol with primary and secondary keys, timestamp assignment, prewrite locking, primary-key commit, stale-lock cleanup, and client aborts. It tracks clients, per-key data versions, locks, committed writes, and auxiliary variables used to check a snapshot isolation condition by comparing commit timestamps against the last observed read timestamp. The spec verifies safety properties including type correctness, write ordering and non-overlap, lock consistency, consistency of committed and aborted transactions, and preservation of snapshot isolation, expressed by a theorem that PercolatorSpec implies these invariants always hold.

603.specification: This module sets up a small model-checking configuration for a percolator-related specification by declaring three clients and three keys, along with a mapping from each client to its primary key. The comments explain that all three clients share the same primary key and are therefore considered symmetric for TLC exploration. The file contains only constant and helper definitions for the model setup; it does not define state variables, actions, temporal behavior, or correctness properties directly.

604.specification: This specification models a simple scenario for the Percolator system, focusing on two concurrent clients each associated with a unique primary key. The model is intended for TLC model checking, as indicated by the comments and the extension of the TLC module. The constants and definitions set up a minimal environment with two keys and two clients, mapping each client to its primary key. No actions, temporal properties, or proofs are defined in this file; it serves as a configuration or parameterization layer for the Percolator module.

605.specification: This specification models the Raft consensus algorithm, a distributed protocol for managing a replicated log across a cluster of servers. The model captures the core Raft roles (Follower, Candidate, Leader), the election process, log replication, and client request handling. It includes detailed state variables for each server, message passing via a bag abstraction, and history variables to support proof obligations. The fault model allows for message duplication, loss, and server restarts, but not Byzantine faults. The temporal property Spec asserts that the system starts in Init and all transitions follow Next, which covers all possible state changes, including network nondeterminism. The design is modular, with helper operators for message handling and log management, and is structured to facilitate both model checking and deductive proofs.

606.specification: This module specifies the Raft-based region merge algorithm used by TiKV for merging two regions, RegionA and RegionB, that are replicated on the same set of stores. It models Raft log replication, client requests, internal merge and rollback requests, message passing via AppendEntries RPCs, and application of committed logs to the state machine, including special admin logs LogPreMerge, LogMerge, and LogRollback. The specification assumes no leader switch, allows a configurable quorum size as a modeling simplification, and checks structural type correctness plus safety invariants about unique leaders, log-prefix consistency, apply/commit ordering, and consistency of merge outcomes across stores.

607.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper module that extends the MultiUser specification and defines several top-level property operators referring to instantiated specifications from that extended module. It introduces a constant-valued operator const_17385913267612000 set to the range 1..2, likely corresponding to a model parameter for user identifiers. The file itself does not define system state variables or transition actions; instead, it collects correctness properties such as SingleUser2!Spec, SingleUser3!Spec, and parameterized SingleUserP(2)!Spec formulas, including quantified variants over singleton sets.

608.specification: This module specifies a resolved timestamp mechanism over a set of region keys RM. It models region-local transaction message generation and application, forwarding of messages through a channel to a resolver, and production of resolved timestamps and commit timestamps into output queues. The specification includes transaction steps such as prewrite, commit, rollback, message application, fetch-ts requests, and resolver-side handling, and it verifies safety properties about commit timestamp consistency, resolved timestamp consistency, and overall type correctness; it also defines a liveness-style leads-to property showing that FetchTS messages can eventually produce a resolved timestamp when no region has an outstanding prewrite.

609.specification: This module specifies the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol with a transaction manager and a set of resource managers. The state tracks each resource manager's local state, the transaction manager's state, the set of participants from which the transaction manager has received prepared messages, and the set of messages that have been sent. The specification proves a safety property: committed and aborted resource-manager states never coexist, by defining an inductive invariant and using TLAPS lemmas and a final theorem to derive []Consistency from Spec.

610.specification: This module specifies a simplified Tendermint consensus protocol with proposer-based timestamps and explicit modeling of local clocks, real time, clock precision, clock accuracy, bounded message delay, and optional clock drift. It models correct and Byzantine processes, tracks proposal, prevote, and precommit messages, and includes actions for sending, receiving, and processing protocol messages, as well as timeout and catch-up behavior. The specification focuses primarily on safety and timing validity properties, asserting agreement on decided values and timestamps and constraints relating decisions to proposal and reception times; it also defines a liveness-style property about timely proposal reception, while noting in comments that deadlock is possible and expected because the emphasis is on safety.

611.specification: This module specifies a simplified Tendermint consensus protocol extended with explicit time, local clocks, a global real-time clock, and proposer-based timestamps. It models correct and Byzantine processes, proposal/prevote/precommit message exchange across rounds, and checks safety-style invariants about agreement on decided values and timestamps, as well as validity relations between decisions and timing bounds. The design includes bounded message delay, clock precision and accuracy assumptions, optional clock drift, explicit bookkeeping for received timely proposals, and liveness-related predicates such as bounded delay and eventual timely proposal reception, but it does not define a temporal Spec formula in this file.

612.specification: This module is a lightweight typedef module that documents a collection of type aliases for a distributed protocol or algorithm using structured comments. The comments define aliases such as PROCESS, VALUE, STEP, ROUND, ACTION, TRACE, and several record-shaped message types including PROPMESSAGE, PREMESSAGE, and MESSAGE. The only actual TLA+ definition in the module is a trivial operator asserting TRUE, so the module serves as documentation-oriented type metadata rather than an executable transition-system specification and it contains no fault model, variables, actions, or temporal properties.

613.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a Tendermint accountability specification. It declares the state variables used by an underlying Tendermint module, instantiates `TendermintAccDebug_004_draft` with a concrete configuration of 4 processes and 1 faulty process, and defines a constant-initialization predicate constraining the proposer function. The file itself does not define the protocol actions or temporal specification; instead, it supplies concrete parameter values for checking safety-related behavior with an arbitrary proposer assignment over rounds.

614.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for an accountable Tendermint-style protocol trace specification. It declares the protocol state variables used by an underlying Tendermint accountability model, fixes concrete process sets, values, and a finite trace through an INSTANCE of another module, and constrains the proposer mapping through a constant-initialization predicate. The file itself does not define protocol actions or temporal properties directly; instead, it supplies concrete parameters and state declarations for replaying a specific finite scenario involving correct and faulty processes and several proposal/prevote/precommit trace events.

615.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a Tendermint accountability/debug specification. It declares the state variables used by the underlying Tendermint model, instantiates another module with concrete process sets, values, and bounds, and adds a constant-initialization constraint for the proposer mapping. The file itself does not define the protocol actions or temporal specification directly; instead, it supplies concrete parameters for a 4-process configuration with named correct and faulty processes, a small value domain, and a maximum round bound.

616.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a Tendermint accountability/debug specification instantiated to a concrete system size. It declares a proposer-selection constant and the state variables used by the underlying Tendermint-style protocol state, then instantiates another module with explicit parameters for one correct process, three faulty processes, a total of four processes, a fault threshold of one, a small value domain, and a bounded maximum round. The only top-level operator in this file is a constant-initialization predicate constraining the proposer mapping to be a function from rounds to all processes; the file itself contains no transition relation, temporal specification, or proof, because those are not syntactically defined here.

617.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a Tendermint accountability specification, specialized to a configuration with 5 processes and 1 faulty process. It declares the state variables used by the underlying Tendermint accountability model, instantiates another module with concrete sets of correct and faulty processes, valid and invalid values, and a maximum round bound, and adds a constant-initialization predicate constraining the proposer function. The file itself does not define transition actions or temporal properties directly; instead, it prepares parameters for checking safety-related behavior of the instantiated Tendermint model.

618.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for an instantiated Tendermint accountability specification. It declares the state variables used by the underlying Tendermint model, introduces a constant proposer function, and instantiates another module with concrete process sets, fault sets, value sets, and a maximum round bound. The only top-level property defined in this file is a constant initialization constraint requiring Proposer to be a function from rounds to all processes; the detailed algorithm, actions, and temporal properties are not defined in this file itself but are delegated to the instantiated module.

619.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a Tendermint accountability specification. It declares a proposer constant, imports an external Tendermint debugging/accountability module by instantiation with concrete sets of correct and faulty processes, concrete valid and invalid values, and a maximum round, and constrains the proposer mapping in a constant-initialization predicate. The file itself contains no transition relation, temporal specification, or proofs; instead, it provides concrete parameters and shared variables intended to match the instantiated Tendermint model, with a single constant-initialization predicate.

620.specification: This module defines debugging-oriented helper definitions for a Tendermint accountability specification, rather than the core protocol itself. It models special initial states with either no injected Byzantine messages or a bounded number of faulty proposals, prevotes, and precommits, and it also defines a transition relation that augments the inherited protocol step relation with extra faulty broadcasts. The module includes simple state predicates used as reachability checks, such as whether no correct process has reached PREVOTE or PRECOMMIT, whether no valid precommit exists, whether all rounds stay below 1, and whether no decision has been made.

621.specification: This module defines an inductive invariant for a Tendermint accountability and agreement model, extending a base Tendermint specification. It characterizes both forked and non-forked behaviors by constraining message sets, process states, locking behavior, and quorum relationships for proposals, prevotes, and precommits. The spec focuses on type correctness and safety-style invariants, and states theorems that the invariant is inductive, that agreement holds when fewer than one third of processes are faulty, and that otherwise accountability captures fork scenarios under a weaker fault bound.

622.specification: This module constrains executions of an existing Tendermint accountability specification so that only a prescribed trace of action names is replayed. It introduces a trace constant and a local replay variable, initializes the replay buffer from the constant trace, and on each next-state step removes the head of the remaining trace while forcing the action name variable to match the expected action. The module is intended for counterexample replay and debugging with Apalache: once the supplied trace is fully replayed, the restricted system deadlocks because no further replay steps are enabled.

623.specification: This module specifies a simplified one-shot Tendermint consensus protocol focused on safety and fork accountability. It models correct and Byzantine processes, message sets for proposals, prevotes, and precommits, and local process state such as rounds, locks, valid values, and decisions. The specification assumes non-deterministic timeouts, a non-deterministic proposer, pre-injected Byzantine messages in the initial state, unit voting power, and identity hashes, and it defines safety properties including agreement, validity, accountability, and several intentionally false invariants used to generate counterexamples demonstrating equivocation or amnesia by faulty processes.

624.specification: This module, named 'typedefs', serves as a collection of type alias definitions for use in other TLA+ specifications. The type aliases are provided in comments using a custom annotation syntax (e.g., @typeAlias), and they define common types such as PROCESS, VALUE, STEP, ROUND, ACTION, TRACE, PROPMESSAGE, PREMESSAGE, and MESSAGE. These aliases map to basic types like Str, Int, and structured record types, as well as sequences. The module itself contains only a single operator definition, TypeAliases == TRUE, and does not specify any algorithm, system behavior, or temporal properties. It is intended purely as a type definition utility for other modules to EXTEND or reference.

625.specification: This module gives a high-level TLA+ model of a Tendermint-style blockchain intended specifically for reasoning about a light client. It models nodes, validator sets, commits, block headers, a global reference clock, and a monotonically growing blockchain up to a bounded ultimate height. The fault model assumes a set of faulty validators drawn from AllNodes, with the set of faulty nodes represented explicitly and intended to be non-decreasing; the initialization constrains each block's validator set so faulty validators remain below a specified threshold ratio, and the spec includes helper predicates for two-thirds commits, trusting-period checks, and whether a light block could be justified by digital signatures.

626.specification: This specification models attacker isolation at a full node after it receives evidence from a light client about conflicting blocks. It assumes a Tendermint-like setting with unit voting power per validator, a trusted common height, a conflicting height, and a violated security model in which Byzantine validators may have signed a conflicting block. The spec initializes an arbitrary blockchain and conflicting evidence, then classifies the attack into Lunatic, Equivocation, or Amnesia cases and computes a set of attackers; it checks invariants asserting that the detected attackers have more than one third of the voting power and that all detected attackers are faulty.

627.specification: This module specifies part of a light client verification interface for blockchain headers, focusing on when an untrusted header can be considered valid relative to a trusted header and what invariants should hold of the light store. It models timing assumptions explicitly through a local clock, trusted and actual clock drift bounds, a trusting period, and validator-set overlap checks based on cardinalities and intersections. The specification defines preconditions and result-valued verification functions, plus store and correctness invariants, and a postcondition for verifying to a target height; it is a state-level specification with no transition system, no temporal Spec operator, and no fault actions, though it refers to peer correctness and faulty validator ratio as part of the intended security model.

628.specification: This module defines a small model configuration for a light client detector scenario over five named nodes. It introduces constant-valued top-level definitions for the validator set, common and conflicting heights, a trusting period, and a faulty ratio, and it declares variables representing a reference blockchain, time, faulty validators, detector state, conflicting evidence, and attackers. The file does not define any transition relation, temporal specification, or proof obligations; instead, it appears to serve as a wrapper or parameter module that instantiates another module named Isolation_001_draft without providing explicit substitutions.

629.specification: This specification models a high-level abstraction of the Tendermint blockchain, focusing on the light client perspective. It assumes all validators have equal voting power and models the blockchain as a sequence of block headers, each containing validator sets, commit sets, and timestamps. The model includes mechanisms for tracking faulty nodes, enforcing a trusting period, and ensuring that blocks are committed with sufficient validator agreement (more than two-thirds). The specification defines initial conditions for the blockchain, constraints on validator sets and faulty nodes, and an action for advancing the global clock. The design is simplified for analysis, omitting some implementation details such as block hashes and focusing on validator set transitions and commit rules.

630.specification: This module is a shallow wrapper around another module instance for a light client detector scenario with three nodes and one faulty validator ratio encoded as <<2, 3>>. It declares concrete configuration values such as the node set, trusted and target heights, clock drift bounds, correctness flags for primary and secondary peers, and the detector state variables. The file itself does not define the transition relation or temporal properties directly; instead, it provides parameterization and state-variable declarations for an instantiated detector module.

631.specification: This module is a thin wrapper around an instantiated light-client detector specification, setting concrete configuration values for a model with three nodes and a target height of 4. It declares constants such as the trusted height, trusting period, clock drift assumptions, whether the primary and secondary are correct, and a faulty ratio, and it declares state variables used by the detector and blockchain model. The file itself contains no top-level Init, Next, Spec, temporal properties, or proofs; instead, it instantiates another module and appears to serve as a parameterized model shell for a faulty-validator scenario.

632.specification: This module defines constants and state variables for a model of a light-client detector interacting with a reference blockchain and fetched light blocks. It models a four-node setting with a designated faulty-validator ratio, trusted and target heights, clock drift assumptions, and booleans describing whether primary and secondary components are correct. The file is only a thin wrapper module that instantiates another module and declares the state vocabulary, but it contains no initialization, next-state relation, temporal specification, or proofs of its own.

633.specification: This module declares constants and state variables for a model of a light client detector interacting with a reference blockchain and tracking fetched light blocks, clocks, faulty validators, and evidence generation. The comments indicate it concerns trusted and target heights, a trusting period, clock drift assumptions versus real clock drift, and whether primary and secondary behaviors are correct, suggesting a fault-detection or evidence-construction scenario for a blockchain light client. The file itself contains only top-level value definitions, variable declarations, and an INSTANCE of another module; it does not define actions, temporal properties, or proofs in this module.

634.specification: This module specifies a light client detector algorithm for Tendermint-style light client verification, based on the referenced English detection specification. The detector compares a target light block obtained from a primary peer with one obtained from a secondary peer and, if they disagree, iteratively searches for evidence by verifying intermediate heights and recording a conflicting block together with a common trusted height. The model includes a faulty validator set bounded by a parameterized faulty ratio, distinguishes correct versus faulty primary and secondary peers, and explicitly models local and reference clocks with drift, including the possibility that clock assumptions are violated. The specification defines initialization, fetching and comparison of light blocks, evidence construction, switching from secondary to primary evidence search, and several invariants about evidence soundness, accuracy, and precision under trusting-period assumptions.

635.specification: This specification models a small supervisory control process with two state variables, state and output. The system starts in an initial state, may either initialize successfully or fail, then cycles through a verification phase and a detector phase, and may eventually produce output or terminate in several terminal states. The file defines the initial predicate, several next-state action operators, a combined Next relation, and a simple invariant asserting that the system has not exhausted peers in either of two failure modes; there are no temporal properties, fairness conditions, proofs, or PlusCal constructs in this draft.

636.specification: This module gives a high-level TLA+ model of a Tendermint-style blockchain intended specifically for reasoning about a light client. It models a bounded blockchain up to an ultimate height, block headers with timestamps, validator sets, next validator sets, and commit sets, together with a global time and a set of faulty validators. The fault model assumes a non-decreasing set of faulty nodes and encodes the Tendermint-style assumption that for blocks still within the trusting period, the correct validators have more than two-thirds of the voting power; it also defines when the system is in a faulty zone where that assumption no longer holds. The specification includes initialization of a complete blockchain structure, a time-advancement action, and an action where one more node becomes faulty, but it does not define a full temporal Spec operator in this file.

637.specification: This specification models a high-level abstraction of the Tendermint blockchain, focusing on the aspects relevant to a light client. It assumes validators have equal voting power and models the blockchain as a sequence of block headers, each containing information about height, time, validator sets, and commits. The model includes faulty nodes, whose set is non-decreasing, and enforces constraints on validator sets and commit quorums, such as the two-thirds majority and limits on faulty validators. The specification defines initialization to a maximal height, actions for advancing time, and predicates for checking trust periods and digital signature validity. The design is simplified for analysis, omitting some implementation details (e.g., hashes) and using sets and records to represent blocks and validators.

638.specification: This module gives a high-level TLA+ specification of a Tendermint-style blockchain model tailored for reasoning about a light client. It models a bounded blockchain up to ULTIMATE_HEIGHT, block headers with timestamps, validator sets, next validator sets, and commit sets, together with a global time and a monotone set of faulty validators. The specification captures a fault assumption that for every still-trusted height, the correct validators have more than two-thirds of the voting power, and it defines helper predicates for supermajority voting, trusting period validity, and whether a light block could be justified by digital signatures. The dynamics in this file are limited to advancing time and adding one more faulty node, while initialization constructs an entire blockchain satisfying timestamp, commit, and validator-power constraints.

639.specification: This module specifies a Tendermint-style light client as a state machine that attempts to verify a target block height starting from a socially trusted header. It models both the light-client local state and an instantiated blockchain environment, including time progression, validator sets, fetched light blocks, verification status, and whether the primary full node is correct or faulty. The specification defines the verification logic, scheduling strategy, store updates, and a single-step system transition, and checks a collection of safety-style invariants and conditional correctness properties about successful verification, faulty primaries, trusting-period expiration, and probe complexity.

640.specification: This module specifies a Tendermint light client verification state machine together with an instantiated blockchain environment. The light client begins from a socially trusted block at TRUSTED_HEIGHT, fetches or reuses light blocks, verifies them via an external verification API, updates a light store and block-status map, and iterates until it either reaches TARGET_HEIGHT successfully or finishes with failure. The model includes clock drift between a local client clock and a reference blockchain clock, a primary that may be correct or faulty, and a faulty-validator ratio parameter; it defines many safety-style invariants about correctness, trust, and stored headers, as well as some expected-to-fail candidate properties and complexity/postcondition checks.

641.specification: This module specifies a state-machine model of a light client that verifies blockchain light blocks between a socially trusted height and a target height, while interacting with an instantiated blockchain environment. The model tracks fetched light blocks, their verification status, the latest verified block, the next height to probe, and a probe counter used for complexity reasoning; it also distinguishes the cases where the primary node is correct versus faulty. The specification defines initialization, a main verification loop, store-update helpers, validity and trust predicates, and a collection of safety-style invariants and implication properties about correctness, trust chains, failure conditions, and worst-case complexity.

642.specification: This module is a configuration-style wrapper for a light client model, declaring concrete constant values, state variables, and an instance of another module named Lightclient_003_draft. It defines a four-node system with trusted and target heights, clock-drift parameters, a boolean flag for primary correctness, and a tuple describing the faulty ratio. The file itself does not define transitions, temporal properties, or proofs; instead, it appears to prepare parameters and variables for reasoning delegated to the instantiated light client module.

643.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper or parameterization module for a light client specification. It defines concrete node names, timing and drift constants, a trusted and target height, whether the primary is correct, and a faulty validator ratio, then declares the state variables used by the modeled light client and blockchain environment. 677.specification: This module defines additional utility operators for bags (multisets) represented as functions from elements to positive natural multiplicities. It extends the standard Bags, Integers, and Folds modules with purely functional operators for adding one occurrence of an element, removing one occurrence, removing all occurrences, mapping and folding over bag contents, and computing bag sums and products. The module is state-free: it declares no constants or variables, no actions, and no temporal properties.

678.specification: This module defines arithmetic characterizations of several bitwise operations on non-negative integers: bitwise AND, bitwise OR, bitwise XOR, bitwise NOT, and logical right shift. The specification is purely functional rather than state-based: it introduces recursive operators that compute results from integer arguments using division, modulus, exponentiation, and recursion over bit positions. There are no variables, actions, temporal properties, fairness conditions, or proofs; the notable design choice is that bitwise operations are encoded mathematically in TLA+ using recursive helper operators and infix top-level operators such as `x & y`, `x | y`, and `x ^^ y`.

679.specification: This module specifies a small library of operators for reading and writing CSV (Comma Separated Values) files from TLA+. The operators are intended to be overridden by Java implementations when executed by TLC. In the TLA+ specification itself, CSVWrite, CSVWriteRecord, and CSVRead all evaluate to TRUE, while CSVRecords returns an arbitrary natural number via CHOOSE n : n \in Nat.

680.specification: This module specifies two basic combinatorial operators over natural numbers: a recursively defined factorial function and a binomial coefficient function choose(n, k). The specification is purely mathematical and contains no state variables, actions, temporal behavior, fault model, or verification properties. It extends Naturals in order to use natural-number arithmetic and defines choose in terms of factorial using integer division and multiplication.

681.specification: This module defines mathematical notions related to derivatives and uses them to specify a higher-order operator for solving ordinary differential equations from initial values. It introduces local definitions for positive reals, open intervals, neighborhoods, first derivatives, and higher derivatives, then defines Integrate(D, a, b, InitVals) by choosing a witness function g satisfying derivative and initial-value constraints over an open interval around the integration endpoints. The file is a pure mathematical specification with no state variables, no transition system, no fairness assumptions, and no temporal verification properties.

682.specification: This module defines basic operations over dyadic rationals, represented as records with integer numerator and denominator fields. It introduces helper operators for divisibility, divisors, greatest common divisor, reduction to lowest terms, recognition of dyadic rationals, addition, halving, and pretty-printing. The specification is purely functional and state-free: it declares no variables, no transition relation, no temporal specification, no fairness conditions, and no proofs; it mainly models arithmetic structure and normalized record-based representations of rationals whose denominators are powers of 2.

683.specification: This module is a TLAPS proof development for theorem properties of finite-set folding operators provided by imported modules, especially FoldSet and derived operators such as SumSet, ProductSet, and MapThenSumSet, as well as Max and Min over integer or natural-number sets. It does not define a transition system or algorithm with variables; instead it proves algebraic, typing, monotonicity, subset, empty-set, nonempty-set, disjoint-union, and extremum properties for these set operators over finite sets. The design relies on proof decomposition, finite-set induction, CHOOSE witnesses for nonempty finite subsets, and previously proved lemmas from imported modules such as FiniteSetsExt, FiniteSetTheorems, and FoldsTheorems.

684.specification: This module is a theorem-only reference specification for properties of finite-set operators defined elsewhere, especially in FiniteSetsExt. It states algebraic and typing theorems about FoldSet, SumSet, ProductSet, MapThenSumSet, Min, and Max over finite sets of naturals and integers, including empty-set cases, non-empty decomposition, disjoint-union laws, subset monotonicity, and interval extrema. The module contains no variables, actions, temporal behavior, or PlusCal algorithm; it is purely a collection of theorem statements intended to accompany proofs in a separate proof module.

685.specification: This module defines a collection of helper operators for finite sets, extending standard set functionality with folds, reductions, aggregation, subset selection, extrema, combinatorial choice construction, and unique selection. It is a library-style module rather than a transition-system specification: it introduces no variables, no actions, and no temporal behavior, and its operators are purely mathematical expressions over sets, functions, and integers. The design emphasizes convenience and backward compatibility, for example by providing aliases like ReduceSet and FlattenSet, while comments also note that some operators are intended to be overridden by more efficient implementations that avoid unnecessary enumeration.

686.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs of theorems about the set-folding operator MapThenFoldSet imported from the Folds module. It proves that the operator is well-defined on finite sets with a choice function for non-empty subsets, characterizes its behavior on the empty and non-empty cases, and establishes extensionality and bijection-based equivalence results. It also proves typing and algebraic properties for associative and commutative folding operators, including add-element and disjoint-union theorems, using induction over finite subsets and well-founded induction; the file is proof-oriented rather than an executable state-machine or temporal-system specification.

687.specification: This module states theorem properties of the basic set-folding operator MapThenFoldSet imported from another module. It does not define the folding algorithm itself; instead, it records reference theorems about the defining equation, empty and non-empty cases, invariance under bijections, equality under pointwise-equal mapping functions, typing, and behavior under associative-commutative operators and disjoint union. The module is proof-oriented and non-temporal: it contains theorem statements with ASSUME/PROVE structure, relies on finiteness assumptions via IsFiniteSet, and leaves actual proofs to a separate proofs module mentioned in the comments.

688.specification: This module defines a general framework for folding operations over sets, allowing flexible element selection and transformation. The main operator, MapThenFoldSet, abstracts the process of folding a set by mapping each element through a function, selecting elements via a user-supplied choice function, and combining results with a binary operator. The comments explain that this operator generalizes folding for sets, functions, and sequences, and that the result may depend on the choice function unless the operator is associative and commutative. The module is intended as a foundational utility for more specialized folding operators in other modules.

689.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs of theorems about functions, injections, surjections, bijections, inverses, restrictions, existence of jections, the Cantor-Bernstein-Schroeder theorem, and folding or summing functions over finite sets. It is a proof-oriented library module rather than a state-machine specification: there are no variables, actions, or temporal behaviors, and the content consists of theorem statements, proof steps, and local proof definitions. The file proves structural facts about function spaces, cardinality-style arguments over finite sets and intervals 1..n, and algebraic properties of FoldFunctionOnSet, FoldFunction, SumFunctionOnSet, and SumFunction under finiteness and associativity/commutativity assumptions.

690.specification: This module states and proves a large collection of theorems about functions and cardinality-style reasoning in TLA+. It covers restriction, range, inverse, injections, surjections, bijections, existence predicates for these notions, transitivity properties, Cantor-Bernstein-Schroeder style results, and facts about finite sets indexed by intervals such as 1..n. It also proves algebraic and typing properties of folding and summing functions over finite sets, including behavior under EXCEPT updates, disjoint union, monotonicity, emptiness, singleton characterization, and constant-valued functions; the module is proof-oriented and contains only theorems, with no state variables, actions, or temporal behavior.

691.specification: This module defines utility operators for reasoning about functions, including restriction by domain or value predicate, checking whether one function is a restriction of another, computing a function's range, pointwise combination, inversion, and properties such as injectivity, surjectivity, and bijectivity. It also defines existence predicates for injections, surjections, and bijections between sets, and provides folding operators over functions by relying on a locally instantiated Folds module.
