1058.specification: This specification models the Dijkstra-Scholten tree algorithm for detecting termination of a diffusing distributed computation over an arbitrary directed process graph. Processes can be active or idle, computation messages flow along graph edges, acknowledgments flow in the reverse direction, and an overlay parent relation is maintained dynamically to form a tree of non-neutral processes rooted at the leader. The spec assumes asynchronous unordered but lossless message delivery, no Byzantine failures, and verifies safety and liveness properties including counter consistency, an overlay-tree invariant, the fact that if the leader is neutral then all other processes are neutral, and the leads-to property that if the computation has terminated then the leader eventually becomes neutral.

1059.specification: This module is a TLC model-checking wrapper around the imported module EWD687a. It supplies concrete model constants for a small process graph with leader L and processes P1, P2, and P3, defines a state constraint bounding message and acknowledgment counters, and states a temporal liveness property requiring that the leader eventually remain terminated forever. It also records a concrete counterexample trace and state set in a PostCondition value, showing the behavior explored by TLC rather than defining the underlying algorithm itself in this file.

1060.specification: This module is a lightweight wrapper around another specification, EWD840, adding Apalache type annotations while keeping the original module unchanged. It declares a constant N and variables active, color, tpos, and tcolor, and then instantiates EWD840, but it does not define any operators, actions, temporal formulas, or properties of its own. Because extraction is limited to constructs syntactically present in this file and excludes inherited content from instantiated or extended modules, this module contains only declarations and no explicit algorithmic behavior or verification assertions.

1061.specification: This module is a thin wrapper around another specification, SyncTerminationDetection, and exists to attach Apalache type annotations without modifying the original specification. It declares a constant N, variables active and terminationDetected, and instantiates the underlying module. The file itself contains no algorithm steps, actions, temporal properties, or proofs; it only provides types and structural linkage for tooling.

1062.specification: This module defines an animation-oriented refinement of the EWD840 token-ring termination detection specification by adding an auxiliary history variable that records the most recent visible event, especially message sends with sender and receiver information. It reuses the underlying algorithmic actions from EWD840, constrains initialization for animation purposes, and builds SVG structures that visualize node state, token position and color, and recently sent messages. The module also defines an animated temporal specification with weak fairness for the system part and an invariant that bounds the exploration depth once termination is detected, in order to obtain interesting simulation traces.

1063.specification: This module defines a JSON-exporting invariant wrapper around an existing EWD840 specification rather than introducing a new algorithm. It relies on definitions imported from the extended module EWD840, especially the invariant Inv, and uses TLC/community-module operators to serialize the execution trace to a JSON file when the underlying invariant is violated. The design intentionally exploits TLC's evaluation of the disjuncts of JsonInv so that, when the real invariant is false, the Export branch writes Trace to trace.json and sets the TLC exit flag, allowing model checking to stop without the usual textual error trace unless that flag is changed.

1064.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the safety and liveness properties of Dijkstra's termination detection algorithm in a ring. It proves type correctness and the main invariant as inductive invariants, derives the safety property that termination is only detected when global termination holds, and then proves liveness using a fairness assumption on the system action together with a three-round argument about token circulation. The module also proves that the concrete algorithm refines a higher-level termination-detection specification, and it is written as a proof module extending another module that contains the actual algorithm definitions.

1065.specification: This module specifies Dijkstra's EWD 840 distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring of N nodes. The system tracks whether each node is active, the color of each node, the position and color of a circulating token, and models both the termination-detection actions and the underlying environment actions such as sending messages and deactivation. The specification checks safety and liveness properties about correct detection of global termination, includes an inductive invariant due to Dijkstra, and uses weak fairness only for the token-handling system actions in the main Spec.

1066.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the synchronous termination detection specification defined in the imported module SyncTerminationDetection. It proves safety properties such as type correctness, correctness of termination detection, and quiescence, and also proves a liveness property showing that once the system is terminated and detection has not yet occurred, the DetectTermination action can lead to terminationDetected becoming true. The file is proof-oriented rather than algorithm-defining: it extends the base specification and TLAPS, uses invariance and temporal proof rules, and introduces one lemma characterizing the enabledness of the DetectTermination action.

1067.specification: This module specifies an abstract termination-detection problem for a ring with synchronous communication. It models a set of nodes indexed by Node, where each node may be active or inactive, and a boolean flag records whether global termination has been detected. The actions allow active nodes to terminate, active nodes to wake up other nodes, and a separate detection step to set the detection flag when all nodes are inactive; the specification also states a fairness condition on the detection action and defines correctness, quiescence, and liveness-style temporal properties.

1068.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs about a high-level TLA+ specification of asynchronous termination detection. It proves type correctness, safety, stability/quiescence, and a liveness property by reasoning about the imported specification's predicates and actions such as Init, Next, DetectTermination, Terminate, RcvMsg, and SendMsg. The module itself is proof-oriented: it introduces lemmas and theorems over the imported state machine, reduces an ENABLED fairness premise to a state predicate, and uses PTL and ExpandENABLED to discharge temporal reasoning obligations.

1069.specification: This module specifies an abstract asynchronous termination detection problem for a ring of N nodes. Each node has an activation status and a count of pending messages, and the system tracks whether global termination has been detected; nodes may terminate, send messages, receive messages, and detection may occur once all nodes are inactive and have no pending messages. The specification checks safety and liveness style properties, including that detection implies actual termination, that termination is stable once reached, and that actual termination leads to eventual detection under a weak fairness assumption for the DetectTermination action; it also includes auxiliary invariants and a state constraint for bounded model checking.

1070.specification: This module demonstrates integrating TLC with third-party tools by exporting counterexamples or error traces. It defines an alternative initial predicate for an imported distributed termination-detection model, a real invariant that fails after a bounded TLC level, and two wrapper invariants that either serialize the TLC trace to JSON or send it to a web endpoint when the real invariant is violated.

1071.specification: This module defines a trace-generation and visualization wrapper around an underlying EWD998ChanID specification. It customizes the initial condition to reduce the number of generated initial states, adds a bounded trace-generation invariant using TLC's current search level, and defines helper operators for extracting a host identifier and producing a JSON-like alias record for ShiViz-style log visualization. The module does not define the core algorithm itself; instead, it relies on the extended base module for the protocol state variables and behavior, while this file focuses on initialization constraints, finite-prefix exploration, and trace post-processing helpers.

1072.specification: This specification models a channel-based version of Dijkstra-Scholten style distributed termination detection derived from EWD998, but using arbitrary node identifiers arranged in a ring instead of natural-numbered nodes. A distinguished initiator circulates a token around the ring while nodes may send and receive payload messages; local counters, node colors, and a vector clock are maintained, and termination detection is based on the token returning white with zero accumulated deficit while the initiator is passive and white. The spec defines initialization, token-passing and environment actions, asserts a weak fairness condition for token-system actions, proves a bounded-round property stating that detection occurs within at most three token rounds after termination, and also includes a refinement mapping to an instantiated EWD998Chan specification plus safety and liveness refinement theorems.

1073.specification: This module specifies trace validation for an implementation of the EWD998 channel-based termination-detection system by relating implementation log entries to steps of a higher-level TLA+ model imported from EWD998Chan. It deserializes a JSON log, reorders distributed log entries into causal order using vector clocks, constrains each trace line to correspond to a particular high-level action or to stuttering for unmodeled termination messages, and uses TLC breadth-first search together with a custom trace view to permit repeated high-level states along the trace. The specification also defines a postcondition TraceAccepted to check that the entire log matches a prefix of some behavior, includes an invariant about failure-free log entries and termination messages, and provides a debugging alias exposing enabledness and selected state information.

1074.specification: This module defines an instrumented and configurable variant of the EWD998 channel-based termination-detection specification for use with TLC trace generation and statistics collection. It adds feature-flag controlled optimizations to token passing, constrains initial simulation states to realistic ones, and defines a behavior specification in which system steps and environment steps evolve under the inherited variables from the base module. The file also configures TLC to run in generation mode, disables deadlock checking because termination is expected, records when termination occurs, and writes per-behavior measurements such as action counts and delay between environment termination and detection to a CSV output.

1075.specification: This module specifies Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring of N nodes. It models message channels explicitly as sequences, distinguishes a circulating token message from ordinary payload messages, and includes both system actions for token handling and environment actions for sending, receiving, and deactivating nodes. The specification checks a refinement to another module EWD998, asserts a temporal specification with weak fairness for the system actions, and adds state and action constraints to bound the state space for model checking.

1076.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the EWD998PCal specification, which is a PlusCal translation of Dijkstra's EWD998 token ring algorithm. In this version, the per-node 'pending' counter and the global 'token' are replaced by a single 'network' variable holding a per-node bag of messages (either payload 'pl' messages or the unique 'tok' message). The refinement mapping recovers the original EWD998 variables from 'network'. The module proves the safety part of the refinement, specifically that the PCal spec refines the original EWD998 spec (Spec => EWD998Spec), focusing on type correctness and the preservation of the unique token property. The proofs include inductive invariants, bag-level reasoning, and per-disjunct case analysis for each possible node action, but the full step-refinement theorem is left as a stub (OMITTED) due to the complexity of the required bag-level lemmas.

1077.specification: This module specifies Safra's distributed termination detection algorithm on a ring of N nodes, based on EWD 998. The PlusCal algorithm models a bag-based message network carrying payload messages and a circulating token with fields q and color; nodes can send payloads, receive payloads, become inactive, pass the token, and the initiator can restart the token circulation depending on token state and local state. The translated TLA+ specification defines the global transition relation, a weak fairness condition for every process action, an instance-based refinement-style comparison to another module EWD998, and a state constraint bounding counters for model checking.

1078.specification: This module defines an SVG-based animation layer for Dijkstra's EWD998 distributed termination detection algorithm, specifically for a ring of nodes that exchange messages and circulate a colored token with an accumulated queue count. It is not the base algorithm itself; instead, it extends an existing channel-based specification and visualizes current and next-state information such as node activity, node color, message counters, token position and color, in-flight versus arriving messages, and global status such as running, terminated, or termination detected. The design emphasizes deterministic rendering, modular visual components, debugger watch support, and TLC alias support for frame-by-frame animation generation.

1079.specification: This module is a TLC scripting specification that orchestrates multiple nested TLC runs of another specification, EWD998_opts.tla, in order to collect statistics and write results to a CSV file. It defines a finite set of feature flags and node values, constructs a CSV filename using the current Java time, writes CSV headers, builds a command line for invoking TLC recursively, and then assumes successful execution of nested runs over all subsets of features and all chosen node values. The specification is not modeling the protocol itself directly; instead, it models an experiment driver that uses IO utilities and TLC-side effects to execute simulations and classify outcomes such as assumption, safety, and liveness violations.

1080.specification: This module defines an options and measurement wrapper around the underlying EWD998 termination-detection specification. It introduces feature flags for several algorithm variants, constrains the randomized initial states and environment behavior for TLC generation mode, and defines an alternative system/environment composition used for simulation and data collection. It also records statistics at termination and when termination is detected, using TLC, CSV, and IO utilities, while assuming probabilistic generation mode and disabling deadlock checking because the modeled algorithm is assumed to terminate.

1081.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs for the EWD998 specification, which models Dijkstra-Scholten style termination detection over a set of nodes with a circulating token, node colors, counters, pending-message counts, and a distinguished master node. The proof development establishes type correctness, an inductive invariant, a safety result connecting the invariant to termination detection, liveness of eventual detection under weak fairness of the System action, and a refinement mapping to a higher-level termination-detection specification instantiated from another module. The file is proof-oriented rather than algorithm-defining: it extends the base specification module and supporting proof libraries, introduces helper algebraic lemmas about fold/sum operators over finite sets, and then proves temporal properties such as invariance, leads-to progress across rounds of the token, overall liveness, and refinement.

1082.specification: This TLA+ specification models Safra's algorithm for distributed termination detection on a ring, as described in EWD 998. The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each of which can be active or inactive, and communicates asynchronously by sending messages. The algorithm uses a circulating token with a color and a counter to detect global termination, ensuring that when the token returns to node 0 in a specific state (white, zero counter, no in-flight messages), all nodes are inactive and no messages are in transit. The model includes both safety (termination detection is sound) and liveness (termination is eventually detected) properties, as well as an inductive invariant capturing the correctness of the token and message accounting. The state space is bounded for model checking, and the module instantiates a generic termination detection specification for comparison.

1083.specification: This module defines a generic operator MapThenFoldSet for folding over a set S by first mapping each element x in S through a function f, then combining the results using a binary operator op, starting from a base value. The folding order is determined by a user-supplied choose function, which selects an element from a set; if op is not associative and commutative, the result may depend on the choice order. The comments explain that this is a generalization of simpler fold operators for sets, functions, and sequences, and provide an example usage. No temporal properties or state variables are present; this is a pure functional operator for set processing.

1084.specification: This module defines a collection of operators for reasoning about functions in TLA+, including restriction, range, pointwise operations, inverses, and properties such as injectivity, surjectivity, and bijectivity. It provides definitions for restricting a function to a subset of its domain or to values satisfying a predicate, checking if one function is a restriction of another, and constructing the range of a function. The module also defines operators for constructing sets of injections, surjections, and bijections between sets, as well as checking for their existence. Additional operators include pointwise combination of functions and folding over function values. The module is utility-focused and does not specify a distributed algorithm or system, nor does it include temporal properties or fault models.

1085.specification: This module is a smoke-test harness specification that orchestrates repeated TLC simulations of another specification, SmokeEWD998.tla, and records outcomes to a CSV file. It defines a CSV filename using the current Java time, writes the CSV header at startup via an ASSUME statement, constructs a Java command line for invoking TLC, and then uses a quantified ASSUME to execute many nested runs over combinations of bug flags and random process counts. The module is not itself a transition-system specification with variables or temporal behavior; instead, it is a scripting-style TLA+ model that uses IOUtils, CSV, and TLC operators to drive external execution, classify exit codes such as assumption, invariant, and property violations, and log them.

1086.specification: This module defines a smoke-testing wrapper around the EWD998 specification. It does not define the full algorithm itself in this file; instead, it redefines the initial predicate through SmokeInit to randomly sample from the space of initial states, while also providing one concrete initial state to ensure at least one initial state always exists. The module also defines a StopAfter helper that uses TLC runtime configuration and statistics to terminate simulation-oriented smoke tests after a short time budget or a bounded number of generated traces, and it includes CHOOSE-based definitions BF and PN derived from environment values.

1087.specification: This module defines a utility predicate for reasoning about finite functional graphs represented by a relation or function r over a set S. The main operator, IsSimpleCycle, characterizes when repeatedly following r from a chosen start node visits exactly the elements of S, using a finite sequence built over 1..Cardinality(S). The module is a helper-style specification with no variables, actions, temporal behavior, fairness, or proofs; it relies on imported modules for integers, sequences, finite-set cardinality, and function-domain/range operators.

1088.specification: This module is an Apalache annotation wrapper around another specification named clean. It adds type annotations in comments for constants and variables so that the original specification can remain free of tool-specific annotations. The module itself declares integer constants DNA and PRIMER, variables tee, primer, dna, template, and hybrid, extends Naturals, and instantiates the module clean, but it does not define any system behavior, actions, temporal specification, or proofs locally.

1089.specification: This module provides Apalache type annotations for another specification named stages by declaring typed constants and variables and then instantiating the stages module. It does not define any behavior, transition relation, temporal specification, or correctness properties of its own. The file is a thin wrapper intended to keep the original specification free of tool-specific annotations while supplying integer and string typing information for analysis.

1090.specification: This module is a TLAPS proof module for the safety properties of the specification in the extended module clean. It proves that the imported specification Spec implies the invariants []TypeOK, []primerPositive, and []preservationInvariant, and adds an explicit assumption that the unconstrained constants DNA and PRIMER are natural numbers so arithmetic facts can be used in the proofs. The file is proof-oriented rather than algorithm-defining: it contains assumptions, one helper lemma about natMin, and three main theorems with structured proofs over the imported actions heat, cool, anneal, extend, and stuttering via UNCHANGED vars.

1091.specification: This module specifies a very abstract model of the PCR cycle, tracking temperature and counts of primers, double-stranded DNA, single-stranded templates, and template-primer hybrids. The system alternates among heating, cooling, annealing, and extension actions, with annealing nondeterministically consuming some number of available primers and templates and extension converting hybrids into DNA. The specification checks basic safety-style properties such as typing, nonnegativity, and a count-preservation invariant, and it also states a liveness property claiming eventual primer depletion, which the comments note does not hold. The model intentionally omits many biochemical details and treats PCR as a coarse state-transition system.

1092.specification: This specification models a PCR-like product generation process across repeated temperature cycles. It tracks temperature, stage, cycle count, primer supply, several classes of single-stranded templates, hybridized intermediates, double-stranded forms, and the final product, with actions for heating, cooling, annealing, and extension. The spec verifies a typed state invariant, imposes weak fairness on each main action in the temporal specification, and includes a safety property stating that no final product exists before the third cycle.

1093.specification: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the type-correctness invariant for the system specified in stages.tla. The main property proved is that the type-correctness invariant TypeOK is preserved by the system's specification Spec, i.e., Spec => []TypeOK. The proof is structured hierarchically and checks that all state transitions maintain the Nat-typedness of the relevant variables, using assumptions about the constants and properties of the natMin function. The proof leverages definitions and actions from the extended stages module and uses TLAPS proof commands and structure.

1094.specification: This specification models a simplified PCR process with explicit thermal stages and molecular counts. The state tracks temperature, remaining primers, double-stranded DNA, single-stranded template, template-primer hybrids, a stage/history variable, and a cycle counter. The design constrains the order of actions through the stage variable so that heating, cooling, annealing, and extension occur in a sensible sequence, and the temporal specification requires weak fairness for each step while checking a type invariant and importing properties from an instantiated clean module.

1095.specification: This module is a thin Apalache type-annotation wrapper around another TLA+ specification, introduced via INSTANCE LamportMutex so that the original specification remains unchanged. It declares constants and variables together with structured type comments for Apalache, but it does not define any behavior, actions, temporal specification, or correctness properties of its own. The file therefore models no standalone algorithm directly; instead, it provides typed declarations intended to be used alongside the instantiated Lamport mutual exclusion specification.

1096.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs for Lamport's distributed mutual-exclusion algorithm, building on a separate LamportMutex specification imported via EXTENDS. It proves type correctness, two inductive invariants about network-message structure and clock relationships, and finally derives the mutual-exclusion safety property. The proof is structured as a hierarchy of lemmas and theorems over the imported state machine, with no PlusCal algorithm in this file and no new system dynamics defined here beyond auxiliary predicates used in the proofs.

1097.specification: This specification models Lamport's distributed mutual-exclusion algorithm from the 1978 paper "Time, Clocks and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System". It represents a set of processes that communicate by pairwise FIFO message queues, using logical clocks, request messages, acknowledgements, and release notifications to coordinate entry into a critical section. The specification defines the initial state, the process actions for sending and receiving protocol messages, a next-state relation, and a temporal specification `Spec == Init /\\ [][Next]_vars`; it also states safety-oriented predicates such as type correctness, a bounded-network property for model checking, a clock bound state constraint helper, and the mutual exclusion invariant `Mutex`.

1098.specification: This module is a small wrapper around an existing LamportMutex specification. It introduces a constant MaxNat, assumes that MaxNat is a natural number, and defines NatOverride as the bounded range 0 .. MaxNat.

1099.specification: This module defines a refinement-oriented extension of a lock specification by adding two auxiliary variables: a history variable h_turn and a stuttering variable s. The purpose is to make the lock specification mimic the finer-grained entry behavior of Peterson's algorithm so that the resulting specification can be related to an instantiated Peterson specification. The module defines initialization, process actions, a next-state relation, a temporal specification, and invariants stating typing and consistency properties of the added auxiliary state, including how stuttering encodes intermediate Peterson control states.

1100.specification: This module specifies an abstract mutual-exclusion lock for two processes. The system is written as a PlusCal algorithm and includes its generated TLA+ translation, where each process cycles through a non-critical location, acquires the lock when it is free, enters the critical section, and then releases the lock. The specification checks basic safety structure through type correctness and an invariant asserting mutual exclusion, and it also states a liveness property that process 1 being at the waiting location "l1" leads to eventually reaching the critical-section location "cs". No fault model is present.

1101.specification: This module specifies Peterson's mutual exclusion algorithm for two processes, including a PlusCal algorithm in comments and its translated TLA+ form. The system state consists of per-process control locations pc, intent flags c, and a shared turn variable; the specification defines the initial state and the step relation over labeled control points a0 through a4 and cs. The module proves an inductive invariant capturing typing, the relation between flags and control locations, and mutual exclusion, and it also defines a refinement mapping to an abstract lock specification via an INSTANCE of Lock. In addition, it states a liveness property asserting that a process waiting at label a3 eventually reaches the critical section cs.

1102.specification: This module defines reusable TLA+ operators for adding an auxiliary stuttering variable `s` to an existing specification, as described in the paper "Auxiliary Variables in TLA+". It provides action transformers that wrap an existing subaction `A` with optional pre-stuttering or post-stuttering behavior, using a record-valued control variable `s` whose fields identify the action, its execution context, and a countdown value. The module also defines conditions ensuring that the decrement function driving stuttering eventually reaches a bottom element, including an alternative version intended to be easier for TLC to evaluate on finite models. The file contains no complete system spec of its own; rather, it is a library module meant to be instantiated by another specification, and it includes comments describing a modification that strengthens context checking during stuttering steps.

1103.specification: This module specifies the non-blocking atomic commitment (NBAC) algorithm with crash failures, based on Raynal 1997, using a TLA+ encoding. The system models processes that vote YES or NO, exchange messages, may crash, and observe a local failure detector that can nondeterministically report whether some process has crashed. The specification defines initialization, per-process steps combining message receipt, failure detector updates, and local transitions, and verifies structural properties such as type correctness and a validity condition relating unanimous YES votes to possible commit outcomes.

1104.specification: This module is an Apalache type-annotation wrapper around another TLA+ specification, introduced by an INSTANCE of nbacg_guer01 so that the original module remains unchanged. It declares the constant N and the state variables used by the wrapped protocol, including sent counters, received counters, failure flags, and a program-counter function pc. The file itself does not define the algorithm, transition relation, or temporal properties syntactically at the module top level.

1105.specification: This module specifies a parameterized asynchronous non-blocking atomic commitment algorithm with failure detectors, based on the algorithm discussed in Guerraoui's paper on failure-sensitive agreement problems. The model tracks how processes initially vote YES or NO, may crash, may become suspected by a failure detector, send messages, receive messages, and eventually either abort or commit. It defines a transition system with weak fairness for non-stuttering process actions, specialized initial conditions where all processes vote YES or all vote NO, a type invariant, and temporal properties for agreement, abort validity, commit validity, termination, and eventual commit.

1106.specification: This module provides Apalache-specific type annotations and concrete constant values for an underlying spanning-tree specification imported via INSTANCE spanning. It declares constants for a process set, distinguished root and no-parent values, and a neighbor relation, along with variables representing parent pointers, reporting flags, and messages. The file itself does not define the algorithm dynamics or temporal properties; instead, it supplies typed parameters and concrete sample values while keeping the original spanning specification separate.

1107.specification: This module is a small model-checking wrapper around another specification named spanning. It defines a single top-level operator, Neighbors, as a concrete set of two pairs, presumably to instantiate or constrain the underlying spanning-system model with a specific graph topology. The file contains no variables, no actions, no temporal specification, and no proofs; it is therefore a very small structural module rather than a full standalone behavior specification.

1108.specification: This module is a TLAPS proof layer for a spanning-tree protocol specification imported from the module spanning. It proves the safety property `Spec => []SntMsg`, where `SntMsg` states that a non-root process whose parent is not yet set has sent no messages. The proof strengthens the invariant with `SentMeansCanSend` and `PrntDomain`, then shows the combined invariant is inductive over `[Next]_vars`; comments also note a design issue in the imported spec's `TypeOK` regarding non-symmetric neighbor relations, so this proof avoids relying on that invariant.

1109.specification: This module specifies a distributed spanning-tree construction over a graph of processes, where processes communicate by recording sent messages in a shared set and adopt a parent when they receive a message. Initially every process has no parent, no process has reported, and no messages have been sent; a process may send to a neighbor if it is the root or it already has a parent, and an unparented non-root process may adopt as parent a sender from which it has received a message. The specification includes a weak fairness condition for the main step relation, a type correctness invariant, a termination property asserting eventual parent assignment for all non-root processes, and a safety-style property stating that once a parent is assigned it never changes.

1110.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper around the imported module sums_even. It introduces a finite bound MaxNat and defines NatOverride == 0 .. MaxNat, together with assumptions that MaxNat is a natural number and that T1 holds. The file itself contains no state variables, actions, temporal specification, or proofs; it primarily constrains constants for checking the underlying imported specification.

1111.specification: This module specifies and proves a simple arithmetic fact over natural numbers: for every natural number x, the sum x+x is even. It defines predicates Even and Odd in terms of the remainder modulo 2, then states the target theorem both directly and as a named theorem T1. The file contains TLAPS proofs, including a one-step proof using Z3 and a more explicit stepwise proof by case distinction on whether x is even or odd.

1112.specification: This module is a thin Apalache-oriented wrapper around another specification named tcp. It provides type annotations for the constant and variables and instantiates the tcp module so that the original tcp specification remains free of tool-specific annotations. The file itself declares the peer set, three state variables representing per-peer control information, connection state, and network contents, and defines one concrete set of peer string values for configuration purposes. It does not define any transition relation, temporal specification, or fault model in this file.

1113.specification: This module, IndInv_apa, encodes an inductive invariant search for a simplified TCP handshake protocol, based on the tcp.tla specification. The goal is to find an inductive strengthening of the original invariant (Inv) that is sufficient for bounded model checking (with MaxLen=4) using the Apalache model checker. The file documents the iterative process of refining the invariant, with each auxiliary clause added to eliminate specific counterexamples. The final candidate invariant, IndInv, is a conjunction of type correctness, queue bounds, the original Inv, and seven auxiliary properties, each justified by the counterexamples they prevent. The module is parameterized by a set of peers and a maximum queue length, and models the state of each peer's TCB, connection state, and network queue. The temporal property of interest is that Spec implies []IndInv, which in turn implies []Inv, for executions where all queues remain bounded.

1114.specification: This module is a model-checking wrapper for a TCP specification imported from the `tcp` module. It introduces two peers and constrains the initial state so that one node starts in `"SYN-SENT"` after an active open while the other starts in `"LISTEN"` after a passive open, with an initial `"SYN"` segment in the network toward the listening side. It also defines additional state constraints that forbid retransmission by requiring adjacent network messages to differ, and forbid any further active opens, passive opens, or sends after the initial setup, reflecting a finite-state design choice suitable for TLC exploration.

1115.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs for a TCP finite-state-machine specification imported from the module tcp, but it only extracts and proves facts stated explicitly in this proof module. It proves safety properties of the imported spec, in particular type correctness (Spec => []TypeOK) and an agreement invariant Inv stating that when both peer-to-peer message queues are empty, the two peers agree on whether they are in the ESTABLISHED state. To carry out the safety proof, it introduces a stronger inductive invariant IndInv with several auxiliary clauses about singleton messages, evidence for ESTABLISHED, and the last message in a queue, and it reasons under the intended two-peer model using choice functions A and B together with finiteness/cardinality assumptions about Peers.

1116.specification: This module models an abstract two-peer TCP finite state machine based on RFC 9293, focusing on connection-state transitions rather than low-level protocol details such as sequence numbers. It represents per-peer TCP control block existence, per-peer connection state, and in-flight network messages as sequences, and models user-triggered actions, protocol-driven state transitions, and reset behavior. The specification checks a state invariant about agreement on the ESTABLISHED state when no messages are in flight, and a liveness property that a peer in SYN-SENT eventually reaches ESTABLISHED, LISTEN, or CLOSED. The design explicitly includes RFC note-inspired transitions such as the FIN-WAIT-1 to TIME-WAIT shortcut and a reset action applicable broadly across states, and it adds weak fairness both for system steps and for a specific user close action to avoid getting stuck in SYN-SENT.

1117.specification: This module defines a recursive bitwise AND operation over integers and introduces an infix operator `&` as a wrapper around that recursive definition. The implementation is intended to be used with a Java operator override in TLC, as explained by the comments, and the comments also document the expected TLC behavior when the override is present or missing. The specification is not a transition-system model with variables or temporal properties; instead, it provides a mathematical/operator-level definition of bitwise conjunction using arithmetic decomposition by powers of two.

1118.specification: This module is a TLC model wrapper for a TLA+ specification of the Towers of Hanoi puzzle. It extends the Hanoi and TLC modules, defines two top-level operators for model parameter constants, and defines one top-level operator that aliases Spec. The file contains no local variables, actions, temporal formulas, fairness conditions, assumptions, proofs, or PlusCal code.

1119.specification: This specification models the Tower of Hanoi puzzle using three towers represented as sequences of natural numbers, where each number denotes a disk size. The initial contents of the three towers are provided by the constants A, B, and C, and the state variable towers stores the current configuration as a 3-tuple of sequences. The spec defines when a move is legal, how a move updates the towers, and a Next action that nondeterministically chooses a legal move. It also includes state invariants checking that the tower structure remains well-typed, that no new disk values are introduced, that the total number of disks remains constant, and a predicate NotSolved describing the negation of the solved configuration.

1120.specification: This module defines an SVG-based animation and visualization layer for a Tower of Hanoi specification. It renders the current state of the Hanoi towers into graphical elements, including tower poles, disks, a title, a step counter, and a success banner when all disks have been moved to the final tower. The module does not define the transition system itself; instead, it depends on state and constants imported from the Hanoi module and provides derived view operators for TLC frame generation and interactive SVG debugging.

1121.specification: This specification models the Towers of Hanoi puzzle with a parameterized number of disks D and towers N. Towers are encoded as natural numbers whose bit patterns represent which power-of-two disk values are present on each tower, and the actions move a smallest available disk from one tower to another when the destination permits it. The spec defines an initial state, a next-state relation over legal moves, a safety-style invariant about preservation of the total disk sum, a type condition over tower values, and a temporal specification Spec asserting Init /\ [][Next]_vars; it also defines NotSolved so TLC can search for a counterexample trace reaching the solved configuration.

1122.specification: This specification models a modified two-phase commit protocol with a transaction manager, multiple resource managers, and a backup transaction manager that can take over if the primary transaction manager becomes hidden after deciding. The resource managers move among working, prepared, committed, aborted, and failed states; the transaction manager decides commit or abort based on global conditions, and optional failures are controlled by the constants RMMAYFAIL and TMMAYFAIL. The spec defines the initial state, the next-state relation, weak fairness for all processes, an eventual termination property, and invariants for type correctness, consistency of decisions, and absence of committed resource managers in NotCommitted.

1123.specification: This module is a thin wrapper around another specification, TCommit, adding Apalache type annotations and a concrete helper definition for the resource manager set. It declares a constant RM and a variable rmState, then instantiates TCommit without any explicit substitutions. The only top-level behavior defined locally is a concrete set RMVal containing three string identifiers, while the actual commit protocol logic and temporal properties are inherited from the instantiated module and therefore are not extracted here.

1124.specification: This module provides a TLAPS proof of the type-correctness invariant (PCTypeOK) for the Paxos Commit protocol, as specified in PaxosCommit.tla. The proof establishes that the type invariant holds throughout all reachable states of the protocol, using an inductive invariant (Inv) that strengthens PCTypeOK with additional properties: AccInv (relating acceptor state fields), MsgInv1b (constraining phase1b messages), and the finiteness of the message set. The proof also includes a well-founded induction argument for the Maximum operator over finite sets of integers, ensuring that the leader's value selection in Phase2a is type-correct. The module contains detailed proofs for initialization, consecution, and auxiliary lemmas, and leverages TLAPS proof commands and structure.

1125.specification: This module specifies the Paxos Commit algorithm, focusing exclusively on safety properties and not liveness. The model simplifies the protocol by letting the variable msgs be the set of all messages ever sent, and does not explicitly model message receipt; instead, actions are enabled based on the presence of messages in msgs. Leader selection is not modeled, and actions that a leader may perform are defined without specifying which process acts as leader. The resource managers (RMs) can spontaneously issue Prepared messages, and Prepare messages are ignored. The specification defines the types and initial states of resource managers, acceptors, and messages, and models the protocol's actions for RMs, leaders, and acceptors. The main temporal property asserts that the protocol maintains type correctness, and the module also asserts that Paxos Commit implements the transaction commit protocol of another module (TCommit) via an INSTANCE statement.

1126.specification: This module provides a TLAPS proof for the TCommit protocol, specifically for the theorem that TCSpec implies that always (TCTypeOK and TCConsistent) hold. The proof is structured hierarchically and refers to definitions and operators from the TCommit module, as well as using the TLAPS proof system. The proof demonstrates that the invariant Inv (which is TCTypeOK and TCConsistent) is preserved by the protocol's initialization and next-state actions, and that the temporal property holds globally.

1127.specification: This specification models the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol for distributed transactions, focusing on the behavior of resource managers (RMs) as they transition through various states: working, prepared, committed, and aborted. The model defines the possible actions each RM can take (Prepare and Decide), and specifies the protocol's next-state relation as the disjunction of these actions for all RMs. The specification asserts type correctness and consistency invariants, ensuring that no two RMs can reach conflicting decisions (i.e., one committed and one aborted), and verifies these invariants as properties of the protocol. The model does not explicitly include faults or failures beyond the abort/commit logic, and does not model a coordinator or message passing.

1128.specification: This module contains TLAPS proofs about a two-phase commit specification imported from the TwoPhase module. It proves that the temporal specification TPSpec implies the type correctness invariant TPTypeOK and also implies the safety property TC!TCConsistent, which states that no resource managers can end in conflicting committed and aborted decisions. To prove consistency, the module defines a strengthened inductive invariant Inv that tracks transaction manager state, prepared messages, decision messages on the wire, and the relationship between local RM states and messages, then proves the invariant is inductive and implies the target consistency theorem.

1129.specification: This specification models the Two-Phase Commit protocol, where a transaction manager (TM) coordinates a set of resource managers (RMs) to implement atomic transaction commit. The protocol is simplified: RMs spontaneously issue 'Prepared' messages, and 'Prepare' messages from the TM to RMs are ignored. Additionally, 'Abort' messages from RMs to the TM are omitted; instead, the TM may spontaneously decide to abort. The model focuses exclusively on safety properties, specifying what is allowed to happen, and omits liveness properties. Communication is modeled by a set of sent messages, with no message loss or removal, and the protocol's type correctness and implementation of a higher-level transaction commit specification are verified.

1130.specification: This specification models a simple bounded FIFO queue of messages. The system starts with an empty sequence, allows sending a message from a fixed message range when the queue length is below a fixed size bound, and allows receiving by removing the head element when the queue is non-empty. The file is designed to stress TLC under anomalous conditions by generating a large state space, and it also states and checks a safety property that every element currently stored in the queue belongs to the allowed Messages set.

1131.specification: This specification models a simple message-shuffling system with four constant message values M0 through M3. The system maintains a set of messages on the left, a set on the right, an iteration counter, and a send count; a Send step moves one message from left to right and increments count, while an Iteration step is enabled when left is empty and moves all right-side messages back to left while incrementing the iteration number. The temporal specification asserts initialization followed by arbitrary Next steps, and the file also defines an invariant stating that the union of left and right always equals the full Messages set, together with a temporal property [] Inv. The design also includes symmetry-related helper definitions using Permutations(Messages), a fixed iteration definition, and a view tuple.

1132.specification: This module defines a set of constants and test data structures for use in model checking, likely in the context of the Promises module. It introduces identifiers, exceptions, and values as constants, and constructs sets and records to represent objects and heaps. The module includes a constant expression that checks membership and reachability of a test object within a test heap, and an ASSUME block that prints the result. There are no temporal properties or actions defined, and the module is primarily intended for constant evaluation and test setup.

1133.specification: This module models heaps, objects, and promise-like objects in an object-capability style setting, including resolved and unresolved promises and actions that resolve or garbage-collect them. It defines the shape of objects, heaps, eventuals, promises, and heap well-formedness conditions such as absence of dangling pointers and acyclicity of promise chains, and it assumes semantic properties of an abstract method evaluator Eval. The file contains state-level structure definitions and three heap-updating actions for resolving when-promises, resolving non-when-promises, and garbage collecting resolved promises, but it does not define a full temporal specification or liveness/fairness properties.

1134.specification: This module defines and reasons about color predicates over a finite set of states. A color predicate is represented as a record with a type field indicating either "every" or "some" and a set field containing a subset of State; satisfaction means either all states in a given state set belong to the predicate set or at least one does, depending on the type. The module proves two theorems: one characterizing satisfaction over unions of state sets, and another showing how to compute satisfaction using bit-vector encodings of state sets based on a finite enumeration of State.

1135.specification: This module specifies the set of possible proof-obligation states for a proof management or proof-coloring system used by the TLA+ Toolbox. It models prover status information from a constant sequence of sequences of strings, defines the space of obligation states including dummy states like "missing" and "omitted" as well as ordinary proof states, and assigns each obligation state a unique consecutive number. The specification also proves that this numbering is well-formed and injective over the set of obligation states, and then instantiates another module to use this state space and its enumeration for color predicates.

1136.specification: This module appears to be a minimal or test TLA+ specification, likely auto-generated or used for model checking infrastructure. It defines a constant set containing the numbers 1 and 2, and a constant expression using a function ExprOfMaxLen with argument 3. There is an ASSUME block that prints a tuple containing a string literal and the previously defined constant expression. The module extends RemoveRedundantParens and TLC, suggesting it is intended for use with the TLC model checker. No temporal properties, state variables, or algorithmic behaviors are specified.

1137.specification: This module models the structure and well-formedness of parenthesis expressions using tokens. It defines a record type Token with a type field (which can be 'left', 'right', or 'other') and an id field. The recursive operator ParenDepth computes the nesting depth of parentheses in a sequence of tokens up to a given index, incrementing or decrementing the depth based on the token type. IsWellFormed checks that a sequence never dips below zero depth and ends at zero, ensuring balanced parentheses. ExprOfMaxLen constructs the set of all well-formed sequences of tokens up to a given length n. The module does not specify a temporal system or algorithm, but rather provides structural definitions for reasoning about parenthesis expressions.

1138.specification: This module specifies and checks an algorithm for removing redundant matched parentheses from a well-formed token sequence representing an expression. It defines a recursive mathematical reference function Result(seq) that repeatedly removes an inner matching parenthesis pair when that pair is immediately enclosed by another matching pair, and then gives a PlusCal algorithm together with its translated TLA+ actions to compute the same result operationally. The specification uses no fault model; instead, it verifies functional correctness by asserting at termination that the algorithm's output out equals Result(in), and it also states the temporal property that the algorithm eventually reaches the control state "Done".

1139.specification: This module is a very small TLC-oriented wrapper that defines a constant expression checking whether `ObjSeq1` satisfies `IsTPSpec`, and then issues an `ASSUME` that prints a tuple containing a marker string and that computed value. It does not define any state variables, transition actions, initialization predicate, or temporal specification of a system execution. The file appears to be a model-evaluation helper module rather than a full algorithm specification, and it relies on definitions imported from extended modules rather than introducing its own system behavior.

1140.specification: This module specifies the mapping between TLA+ and PlusCal (PCal) code regions, focusing on the syntactic correspondence between regions in the TLA+ specification and their representation in PlusCal. It defines data structures for locations, regions, and translation objects (TPObject), and provides predicates to check well-formedness and ordering of these objects in sequences. The specification includes detailed invariants for matching parentheses, token ordering, and the structure of translation sequences, supporting the correctness of TLA-to-PlusCal translation tools. The design is intended for use in debugging and verifying translation mappings, with additional constructs for simplified debugging scenarios.

1141.specification: This TLA+ specification file is named MC and appears to be a stub or template for a specification, as it contains only module headers, EXTENDS statements, and comments. The EXTENDS clause brings in TLAToPCal and TLC, suggesting the intent to use PlusCal translation and TLC model checking, but no actual specification, variables, constants, or operators are defined. The only comment is a modification history noting the creation date and author. No algorithm, system, or properties are specified in this file.

1142.specification: This module specifies the mapping between TLA+ and PlusCal (PCal) code regions, focusing on the translation of syntactic regions and their correspondence. It defines data structures for locations, regions, and translation objects, and provides predicates for well-formedness and ordering of these objects. The module includes a PlusCal algorithm (translated to TLA+) that, given a region in the TLA+ spec, computes the corresponding token positions and analyzes parenthesis depth, ensuring correct mapping and well-formedness. The specification is primarily concerned with syntactic correctness and region mapping, not with distributed or fault-tolerant algorithms. It verifies properties such as proper parenthesis matching, token ordering, and correct region-to-token mapping, and includes assertions to check these properties during execution.

1143.specification: This module specifies data structures and algorithms for mapping a region in a TLA+ specification to corresponding PlusCal source structure, using token regions, parentheses, and breaks to describe translation correspondence. It defines location, region, token, and TPSpec well-formedness predicates, along with helper operators such as parenthesis-depth computation and region-to-token-pair selection. The file also contains a PlusCal algorithm and its generated TLA+ translation for computing the token pair selected by an input region and then scanning the token interval to compute depth information, with a temporal specification asserting the translated algorithm and a termination property.

1144.specification: This module specifies Bloemen et al.'s multi-core on-the-fly strongly connected components decomposition algorithm on a directed graph whose nodes and edges are given as constants. The file contains a commented PlusCal algorithm and its generated TLA+ translation, modeling shared union-find state, per-thread search state, and a work-stealing style exploration in which multiple threads cooperatively discover and merge SCC candidates while marking sets dead when fully explored. The specification defines the operational behavior with Init, Next, and Spec, adds weak fairness for both the main thread process action and the unite procedure, asserts a termination property as an eventuality that all program counters become Done, and defines a safety/correctness condition stating that upon termination the SCC partition computed by the algorithm matches the mathematical SCC decomposition by reachability.

1145.specification: This module is a small model-checking helper module that augments an underlying specification imported from other modules. It defines a symmetry set for threads using permutations of Threads and defines the Cartesian product of Nodes with itself as the set of all directed edges between nodes. The file itself contains no variables, no actions, no temporal specification, and no proofs; it serves only as a thin wrapper of two top-level value definitions.

1146.specification: This specification models the Apache BookKeeper protocol for the lifetime of a single ledger, including ledger creation, normal add-entry writes, ensemble changes after write failures, ledger closing, and ledger recovery by other clients. It models metadata state, per-bookie storage and fencing state, and per-client local state, with asynchronous message-passing actions for requests and responses. The spec checks typing and safety invariants about truncation, readability, dirty reads, quorum replication, and ordering, and it also includes liveness assertions that under weak fairness of Next the ledger is eventually closed.

1147.specification: This module, named MC, is intended to model check or analyze the BookKeeperProtocol. It extends three modules: BookKeeperProtocol (presumably containing the main protocol logic), TLC (for model checking constructs), and stats (likely for statistics or auxiliary definitions). The file contains only module headers and comments, with no operator, variable, or constant definitions. There are no temporal properties, actions, or state predicates defined in this file. The module serves as a wrapper or configuration module, possibly for use with TLC or as a placeholder for further specification.

1148.specification: This module specifies a message-passing abstraction in which messages are stored in a state variable as a function from message values to delivery counts. It models delivery, loss, timeout detection, processing, and sending of requests and responses, with message loss represented by a count of -1 and processed messages represented by decrementing or clearing counts. The module provides helper predicates and actions for identifying receivable messages, clearing or ignoring timed-out or superseded messages, and sending messages to a single recipient or an ensemble, but it does not define a full temporal system specification in this file.

1149.specification: This specification models Dijkstra's token-based distributed termination detection algorithm (EWD840). The system consists of N nodes arranged in a ring, each of which can be active or passive and colored white or black. A token circulates among the nodes, carrying a color (white or black) and a position. The algorithm ensures that global termination is detected when all nodes are passive and the token returns to node 0 as white. The model includes actions for initiating a probe, passing the token, sending messages (which can activate other nodes and stain the sender black), and deactivating nodes. The specification verifies type correctness, safety (termination detection), and liveness (eventual detection of termination), and explores the effect of different fairness conditions. Notable design decisions include the use of a weakened fairness condition (WF_vars(System)) to avoid undesired liveness properties, and the explicit modeling of node and token colors to capture the algorithm's correctness arguments.

1150.specification: This module, named MC, serves as a wrapper or configuration module for a model checking run. It defines a constant value (const_1515403233990126000) set to 12, likely as a model parameter, and a specification operator (spec_1515403233990127000) that refers to Spec, which is presumably defined in an extended module (EWD840). The module extends EWD840 (which likely contains the main algorithm), TLC (for model checking), and stats (possibly for statistics gathering). No variables, actions, or temporal properties are defined directly in this file; it is intended to configure or parameterize a model rather than specify an algorithm itself.

1151.specification: This module is a TLC model-checking wrapper module for another specification, rather than the primary algorithm specification itself. It extends the modules ghostferry, TLC, and stats, introduces model values r0, r1, and r2, and defines concrete constant values and model-checking bindings such as a record set, a maximum primary key, an initial table, and a maximum binlog size. It also binds the checked behavior to Spec, the action constraint to BinlogSizeActionConstraint, the invariant to SourceTargetEquality, and the temporal property to Termination, but it does not define those underlying operators in this file because they come from extended modules.

1152.specification: This specification models a simplified version of the Ghostferry data-copying algorithm that copies a source database table to a target database while concurrently streaming and applying binlog entries. The model represents the system as four processes: a table iterator that copies rows, a binlog streamer that replays source updates onto the target, an application that performs concurrent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE-style changes on the source and appends corresponding binlog entries, and a ferry coordinator that performs cutover by making the application read-only and then stopping binlog streaming after a target position is reached. The spec checks a liveness-style termination property and a safety property asserting that once all processes are done, the source and target tables are equal; it also uses fairness assumptions for all four processes and an action constraint to bound binlog growth for model checking feasibility.

1153.specification: This specification models a simple parameterized state machine over an array-like function x and a selector variable y. Initially, x maps every element of a non-contiguous domain Dom to 0, and y is chosen from 1..C, yielding C possible initial states that form isomorphic disjunct subgraphs as noted in the comments. Each next-state step leaves y unchanged, chooses an index i in Dom, increments x[i] modulo K, and additionally requires the existence of a subset s of 1..L whose cardinality is L; the comments explain that this construction is intentionally expensive because TLC must explore SUBSET (1..L) and compute cardinalities, making a single next-state evaluation asymptotically proportional to 2^L while the total state space is K^N.

1154.specification: This module, named MC, serves as a specification that extends the Grid5k and stats modules. The file itself contains no operator definitions, variable or constant declarations, or temporal properties. It appears to be a placeholder or a module intended to aggregate or reuse definitions from the extended modules. There are no comments or further documentation in the file, and no algorithm or system is directly specified here. All modeling and verification content is expected to be inherited from the EXTENDS modules.

1155.specification: This specification models a simple system where a variable x is an array indexed by a domain Dom, which is a union of two integer ranges. The system repeatedly increments x[i] modulo K for some i in Dom, and in each step, it awaits the existence of a subset s of 1..L with cardinality L. The variable y is also present and can take values in 1..C, allowing for multiple initial states. The comments explain the state space size and the computational cost of evaluating the next-state action, emphasizing the exponential blowup due to the power set operation. The spec is designed to stress-test model checking tools like TLC, especially with respect to set and function operations.

1156.specification: This module is a TLC model wrapper for a Raft-related specification imported from the extended module RaftMongo. It declares concrete model values for the Value and Server constants, defines a symmetry set over the servers, adds a state constraint bounding the global current term and log lengths, and maps the model's specification and invariant to names from the imported module. The temporal behavior itself is not defined in this file; instead, the file syntactically references Spec and NeverRollbackCommitted from the extended specification while providing model-specific constants and TLC configuration operators.

1157.specification: This specification models a simplified Raft-style consensus protocol for MongoDB, focusing on server roles, term numbers, and replication or rollback of per-server oplogs. The model represents each server's state and log, allows a server to become primary by a quorum-based up-to-date check, allows leaders to append client values, and allows followers to append or roll back log entries to match another server. The specification verifies the system through an initial-state predicate and a temporal next-state specification, and it also defines helper safety predicates about committed entries never being rolled back, though those verification predicates are not included in the top-level temporal specification.

1158.specification: This module is a TLC model-checking wrapper for a Paxos Commit specification. It instantiates model values and named constant definitions for acceptors, resource managers, ballots, and majorities, then points TLC to an existing specification and properties defined in extended modules rather than defining the protocol behavior locally. The file also declares a symmetry set and selected correctness targets, but it does not itself define the algorithm's actions, state variables, temporal behavior, or proofs; those come from the extended modules and are therefore out of scope for extraction here.

1159.specification: This module specifies the Paxos Commit algorithm, modeling resource managers, acceptors, and leaders using a safety-only TLA+ specification. The model simplifies communication by representing msgs as the set of all messages ever sent, not explicitly modeling message receipt, and not modeling leader selection, so any process may act as leader. It defines the protocol actions for resource managers, leaders, and acceptors, gives an initial-state predicate and next-state relation, and proves that the resulting specification preserves a type-correctness invariant and implements the transaction commit specification from module TCommit.

1160.specification: This module specifies the Two-Phase Commit (2PC) protocol for distributed transactions, focusing on the behavior of resource managers (RMs). The protocol is modeled by tracking the state of each RM, which can be 'working', 'prepared', 'committed', or 'aborted'. The specification defines the possible actions (Prepare and Decide) that RMs can take, the initial state, and the next-state relation. It asserts type correctness and consistency invariants, ensuring that no two RMs reach conflicting decisions (i.e., one aborts while another commits). The main temporal property proved is that the type correctness and consistency invariants always hold under the protocol's specification.

1161.specification: This module, named MC, is a model configuration file for a Paxos-based consensus protocol, as indicated by its extension of the PaxosMadeSimple module. It defines model constants for acceptors and values, as well as symmetry and quorum sets for use in model checking. The specification references the main Spec and Correctness properties from the underlying protocol module, and includes configuration for symmetry reduction and quorum selection. The file is intended for use with TLC and includes no algorithmic or temporal logic beyond referencing the main protocol's specification and invariants.

1162.specification: This module specifies Lamport's Paxos consensus algorithm in the style of "Paxos Made Simple", modeling leaders by ballot number and acceptors as separate processes. It uses a message-history style model in which the variable msgs contains all messages ever sent, rather than explicitly modeling channels, message loss, or delivery; safety is expressed over what may be received from that history. The specification defines the translated PlusCal state machine, a type invariant, predicates describing when a value is chosen, and a correctness property asserting agreement-like uniqueness of chosen values; it also includes a theorem claiming that correctness is always true, with comments noting that the theorem is actually false for the current spec and should be checked with TLC.

1163.specification: This module specifies a simple event-counting component with a single state variable nEvents. It models a counter that starts at zero and may be incremented by the CountEvent action when a finite maximum is being enforced; if maxEvents is -1, the specification treats that as an unlimited mode and leaves the counter unchanged to avoid introducing an infinite-state model. The file defines the initialization predicate and one action, but it does not define a full temporal specification such as Spec, nor does it include fairness conditions, proofs, or PlusCal code.

1164.specification: This module is a thin model-checking wrapper module named MC. It extends the modules SwarmKit and stats and contains no additional declarations, operators, assumptions, temporal properties, or proofs. Because the file has no body beyond the module header and EXTENDS clause, it does not itself specify behavior; any actual system modeling resides in the extended modules, which must not be extracted here.

1165.specification: This module specifies a TLA+ model of Docker SwarmKit at a high level, combining user actions, orchestrator behavior, allocation, scheduling, worker behavior, and reaping of tasks. It models services and tasks, including replicated and global services, task replacement, cleanup of terminated tasks, service removal, task scheduling to nodes, and convergence toward a desired running configuration. The spec uses weak fairness for core progress actions and verifies type correctness, a task-transition sanity property, and a liveness-style property asserting that unless disruptive events continue forever, the system eventually stabilizes in the desired state.

1166.specification: This module specifies a task lifecycle system in which a variable `tasks` stores the currently allocated tasks, and tasks progress through a fixed transition table managed by different components such as the orchestrator, allocator, scheduler, agent, and reaper. The specification defines typing constraints for `tasks`, a state update action-like operator `UpdateTasks` that replaces existing tasks according to a function while preserving task identity, and a constructor `NewTask` for creating new task records from service, slot, id, and desired state information. It also defines a transition table and asserts a consistency property `TransitionTableOK` requiring monotonic state progression and non-overlapping ownership of source states across components, with limited exceptions for reaper cleanup; the file contains an ASSUME that asks TLC to check this property.

1167.specification: This module defines core types and helper operators for a task orchestration model resembling SwarmKit task management. It declares abstract constants for nodes, services, task IDs, and a replica bound; defines record types and task lifecycle states; and provides helper operators for state ordering, task identity, and virtual slots. The module contains no variables, actions, temporal formulas, fairness conditions, or PlusCal algorithm.

1168.specification: This module specifies a lower-level worker-node implementation for SwarmKit that refines a higher-level worker specification by explicitly modelling container state in addition to task state. It models worker and environment actions such as task creation and updates, manager synchronisation, container shutdown and exit, node connectivity changes, orphaning tasks when a node stays down, and worker reboot. The spec verifies that the implementation implies the higher-level worker behavior and includes temporal properties with weak fairness on agent progress actions; it also contains a theorem explaining why proving the implementation and system properties in two stages is sufficient.

1169.specification: This module specifies the worker-side behavior of a task orchestration system, modeling how nodes are seen by SwarmKit as either up or down and how tasks assigned to nodes progress through lifecycle states. It defines actions for normal task progress, shutdown completion, task rejection, container exit reporting, node disconnection and reconnection, and orphaning runnable tasks on nodes that remain down. The module is focused on state-transition behavior and action decomposition, and it does not itself define a temporal specification or verification theorem in this file.

1170.specification: This module models a small TLC-driven benchmarking harness that runs a fixed collection of TLA+ specifications sequentially with different worker counts and classifies the outcome of each run by the external process exit code. The state records the selected run number, worker count, benchmark spec name, and an IO process record, and the main action either launches TLC through an IOUtils environment-execution primitive or observes one of several terminal outcome classes: done, safety violation, liveness violation, or other violation. The file is not a protocol or fault-tolerant algorithm specification itself; instead it is an orchestration specification for executing model-checking jobs, using TLC and IO utilities, with deadlock checking disabled in the embedded TLC config block.

1171.specification: This module is a TLC utility specification that collects model-checking run statistics and writes them to a CSV file. It initializes the CSV output by writing a header row if the file is empty, and it defines a postcondition that records metadata about the current run, TLC revision/configuration information, and search statistics such as diameter, generated states, distinct states, queue size, and duration. The module is not a state-transition system with variables or temporal behavior; instead, it uses assumptions and constant operator definitions to orchestrate side-effecting tool calls through TLC, IOUtils, and CSV operators.

1172.specification: This specification defines a very small TLA+ module with one constant and one operator. The operator Bar takes an argument y and constructs a two-element tuple containing the module constant C and the argument y. The module does not define any state variables, actions, temporal behavior, fault model, or verification properties; it is purely a structural value definition.

1173.specification: This specification defines a very small module with a single constant C and one top-level operator Def(a). The operator constructs a labeled tuple expression lab :: <<C, a>>, so the module appears to model a simple labeled value built from the constant C and a parameter a rather than a full transition system. There are no variables, no actions, no temporal specification, no fairness conditions, and no proof content in the file.

1174.specification: This specification defines a very small TLA+ module named Foo. It declares an operator Proc as the integer range 1..5 and includes a single assumption that invokes PrintT on that set. The module has no state variables, actions, temporal formulas, fairness conditions, or proofs.

1175.specification: This module is a minimal TLA+ test specification intended to exercise tooling behavior around model-checking or parsing rather than to model a substantive distributed algorithm or protocol. The comments indicate that it is related to generating parsing errors in an MC file, including malformed expressions in a spec and multiply defined symbols in another model configuration. Syntactically, the module declares one constant and one variable, and defines a single constant operator foo equal to 1; it contains no actions, no temporal specification, no fault model, and no verification properties.

1176.specification: This specification defines a minimal TLA+ module containing a single state variable x and one constant-valued operator foo equal to 1. The comments indicate the file is intended to trigger TLC error behavior related to configuration files and temporal formulas containing actions, but the module itself does not define an initial predicate, next-state relation, or complete temporal specification. It therefore models no full algorithm or protocol, and instead serves as a tiny test artifact illustrating tooling behavior.

1177.specification: This specification is a minimal test module intended to generate errors that TLC finds when evaluating assumptions. The module declares one state variable x and one constant WhichTest, but it does not define any state-transition system, initialization predicate, next-state action, or temporal specification.
